Continue here when the core calculations and the certificate assumptions are clear. Use the graded questions above as a warm-up; the original derivations below remain available in full.

Exercise 15.1 — Derive the IBP affine rule and exhibit its joint looseness

(a) Let $a\in[\underline a,\overline a]$ and $z=Wa+b$. Derive the interval $[\underline z,\overline z]$ produced by IBP and show that each coordinate bound is attained. (b) For $W=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}$, $b=0$ and $a\in[-1,1]^2$, describe the true image $\{Wa\}$ and find a point of the IBP box that is not in it.

Show answer

(a) Write $a=\mu+\delta$ with $\mu=\tfrac12(\overline a+\underline a)$, $|\delta_j|\le r_j=\tfrac12(\overline a_j-\underline a_j)$. Then $z_i=W_{i,:}\mu+b_i+W_{i,:}\delta$ and $|W_{i,:}\delta|\le\sum_j|W_{ij}||\delta_j|\le\sum_j|W_{ij}|r_j=(|W|r)_i$ (triangle inequality, then $|\delta_j|\le r_j$). So $\underline z=W\mu+b-|W|r$, $\overline z=W\mu+b+|W|r$. Choosing $\delta_j=r_j\,\mathrm{sign}(W_{ij})$ makes every term $|W_{ij}|r_j$ and this $\delta$ is feasible, so $\overline z_i$ is attained; $\delta_j=-r_j\,\mathrm{sign}(W_{ij})$ attains $\underline z_i$.

(b) $\mu=0$, $r=(1,1)$, $|W|r=(2,2)$: IBP gives $z\in[-2,2]^2$. The true image is the set of $(a_1+a_2,\,a_1-a_2)$ with $|a_i|\le1$, a square rotated by $45^\circ$ with vertices $(\pm2,0)$ and $(0,\pm2)$ (equivalently $|z_1|+|z_2|\le 2$). The IBP corner $(2,2)$ would need $a_1+a_2=2$ and $a_1-a_2=2$, i.e. $a_1=2$, which is infeasible. The box has area 16, the image has area 8: IBP doubles the area in a single layer, and the next layer may combine $z_1=2$ with $z_2=2$ as if both were reachable at once.

Exercise 15.2 — CROWN bounds for the walkthrough network at other radii

Repeat the walkthrough for the same network and $x_0=(1,1)$ with (a) $\varepsilon=0.5$ and (b) $\varepsilon=1.5$: give the pre-activation bounds, the neuron statuses, the IBP interval, the adaptive-CROWN interval, the α-CROWN lower bound and the exact range. Check with Panel A.

Show answer

(a) $\varepsilon=0.5$: $r=|W|(0.5,0.5)^{\top}=(1,1.5)$, so $z_1\in[2,4]$, $z_2\in[0.5,3.5]$: both neurons stable active. IBP: $a_1\in[2,4]$, $a_2\in[0.5,3.5]$, $f\in[-8+1,\,-4+7]=[-7,3]$. CROWN needs no relaxation: $f=-2z_1+2z_2=-4x_1+2x_2$ exactly, $\Omega=(-4,2)$, $\Omega x_0=-2$, $\|\Omega\|_1=6$, so $f\in[-2-3,\,-2+3]=[-5,1]$, which is also the exact range (attained at $(1.5,0.5)$ and $(0.5,1.5)$). Lesson: IBP is loose even without any unstable neuron, purely through the joint-box effect of Exercise 15.1; CROWN is exact for an affine function.

(b) $\varepsilon=1.5$: $r=(3,4.5)$, $z_1\in[0,6]$ (stable active, $l_1=0$), $z_2\in[-2.5,6.5]$ (unstable). IBP: $a_1\in[0,6]$, $a_2\in[0,6.5]$, $f\in[-12,13]$. Adaptive CROWN: $u_2=6.5\ge|l_2|$ so $\alpha=1$; lower line $z_2$, upper chord $\tfrac{6.5}{9}(z_2+2.5)$. Lower bound: $f\ge-2z_1+2\alpha z_2$ with $\Omega=(-2-2\alpha,\,-2+4\alpha)$, $c=-2+2\alpha$, giving $\gamma^L(\alpha)=-6+4\alpha-1.5\,(2+2\alpha+|4\alpha-2|)=-9+\alpha-1.5|4\alpha-2|$: $\gamma^L(1)=-11$ (CROWN), $\gamma^L(0)=-12$ (= IBP), maximum $\gamma^L(\tfrac12)=-8.5$ (α-CROWN). Upper bound: $\Lambda=(-\tfrac{31}{9},\tfrac89)$, $c_U=\tfrac{55}{18}$, $\Lambda x_0+c_U=\tfrac12$, $\gamma^U=\tfrac12+1.5\cdot\tfrac{39}{9}=7$. Exact: on $\{z_2\ge0\}$, $f=-4x_1+2x_2$ with minimum $-8.5$ at the kink point $(2.5,0.75)$ and maximum $7$ at $(-0.5,2.5)$; on $\{z_2\le0\}$, $f=-2x_1-2x_2-2\ge-8.5$. So exact $=[-8.5,7]$, α-CROWN $=[-8.5,7]$, CROWN $=[-11,7]$, IBP $=[-12,13]$.

Exercise 15.3 — Prove the split-conformal coverage bound

Let $s_1,\dots,s_n,s_{n+1}$ be exchangeable, almost surely distinct scores ($s_{n+1}$ is the test score) and $\hat q=s_{(k)}$ with $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil\le n$. (a) Prove $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)=k/(n+1)$. (b) Deduce $1-\alpha\le\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)\lt1-\alpha+\tfrac1{n+1}$. (c) For $n=9$, $\alpha=0.1$, what is $\hat q$ and what is the exact coverage? (d) Why does the lower bound survive ties while the upper bound may not?

Show answer

(a) Let $\rho$ be the rank of $s_{n+1}$ among the $n+1$ scores. Exchangeability means the joint law is invariant under permutations, so $\mathbb P(\rho=r)$ is the same for every $r\in\{1,\dots,n+1\}$, hence $1/(n+1)$. The event $s_{n+1}\le s_{(k)}$ (the $k$-th smallest of the other $n$ scores) means that at most $k-1$ of the others are smaller than $s_{n+1}$, i.e. $\rho\le k$. Therefore $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)=\mathbb P(\rho\le k)=k/(n+1)$.

(b) By definition of the ceiling, $(n+1)(1-\alpha)\le k\lt(n+1)(1-\alpha)+1$; divide by $n+1$.

(c) $k=\lceil 10\cdot0.9\rceil=9$: $\hat q$ is the largest calibration score and the coverage is exactly $9/10=0.9$ (the prediction set is as tight as the guarantee allows, but only because $(n+1)(1-\alpha)$ is an integer; for $n=10$ one gets $k=\lceil9.9\rceil=10$ and coverage $10/11\approx0.909$).

(d) With ties, attach an independent uniform tie-breaker $U_i$ to every score and order the pairs $(s_i,U_i)$ lexicographically. The pairs are exchangeable and almost surely distinct, so by (a) the rank $\rho$ of the test pair satisfies $\mathbb P(\rho\le k)=k/(n+1)$. If $\rho\le k$, at most $k-1$ calibration pairs precede the test pair, so at most $k-1$ calibration scores are strictly smaller than $s_{n+1}$ and $s_{n+1}\le s_{(k)}=\hat q$. Hence $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)\ge k/(n+1)$: the lower bound is safe. The converse fails: a test score tied with $s_{(k)}$ is covered even when its tie-breaker ranks it after position $k$, and the probability can exceed $k/(n+1)$ by the mass of ties at $s_{(k)}$; the upper bound $1-\alpha+\tfrac1{n+1}$ therefore requires a continuous score distribution or randomised tie-breaking in the prediction set itself. In the extreme case of a constant score, $\mathcal C$ always contains everything and coverage is 1.

Exercise 15.3 — Prove the split-conformal coverage bound

Let $s_1,\dots,s_n,s_{n+1}$ be exchangeable, almost surely distinct scores ($s_{n+1}$ is the test score) and $\hat q=s_{(k)}$ with $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil\le n$. (a) Prove $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)=k/(n+1)$. (b) Deduce $1-\alpha\le\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)\lt1-\alpha+\tfrac1{n+1}$. (c) For $n=9$, $\alpha=0.1$, what is $\hat q$ and what is the exact coverage? (d) Why does the lower bound survive ties while the upper bound may not?

Show answer

(a) Let $\rho$ be the rank of $s_{n+1}$ among the $n+1$ scores. Exchangeability means the joint law is invariant under permutations, so $\mathbb P(\rho=r)$ is the same for every $r\in\{1,\dots,n+1\}$, hence $1/(n+1)$. The event $s_{n+1}\le s_{(k)}$ (the $k$-th smallest of the other $n$ scores) means that at most $k-1$ of the others are smaller than $s_{n+1}$, i.e. $\rho\le k$. Therefore $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)=\mathbb P(\rho\le k)=k/(n+1)$.

(b) By definition of the ceiling, $(n+1)(1-\alpha)\le k\lt(n+1)(1-\alpha)+1$; divide by $n+1$.

(c) $k=\lceil 10\cdot0.9\rceil=9$: $\hat q$ is the largest calibration score and the coverage is exactly $9/10=0.9$ (the prediction set is as tight as the guarantee allows, but only because $(n+1)(1-\alpha)$ is an integer; for $n=10$ one gets $k=\lceil9.9\rceil=10$ and coverage $10/11\approx0.909$).

(d) With ties, attach an independent uniform tie-breaker $U_i$ to every score and order the pairs $(s_i,U_i)$ lexicographically. The pairs are exchangeable and almost surely distinct, so by (a) the rank $\rho$ of the test pair satisfies $\mathbb P(\rho\le k)=k/(n+1)$. If $\rho\le k$, at most $k-1$ calibration pairs precede the test pair, so at most $k-1$ calibration scores are strictly smaller than $s_{n+1}$ and $s_{n+1}\le s_{(k)}=\hat q$. Hence $\mathbb P(s_{n+1}\le\hat q)\ge k/(n+1)$: the lower bound is safe. The converse fails: a test score tied with $s_{(k)}$ is covered even when its tie-breaker ranks it after position $k$, and the probability can exceed $k/(n+1)$ by the mass of ties at $s_{(k)}$; the upper bound $1-\alpha+\tfrac1{n+1}$ therefore requires a continuous score distribution or randomised tie-breaking in the prediction set itself. In the extreme case of a constant score, $\mathcal C$ always contains everything and coverage is 1.

1. Choose a nonconformity score $s(x,y)\in\mathbb R$: large when the model’s prediction at $x$ disagrees with $y$ (e.g. $|y-\hat f(x)|$ for regression; $1-\hat f_y(x)$ for classification, with $\hat f_y(x)=e^{z_y}/\sum_j e^{z_j}$ the softmax probability of class $y$ computed from the model’s logits $z_j$ at $x$, Primer E).
  2. On a calibration set $(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n$ not used for training, compute $s_i=s(X_i,Y_i)$.
  3. Let $\hat q$ be the $\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil/n$ empirical quantile of $s_1,\dots,s_n$: sort the scores and take the $k$-th smallest with $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil$ ($\hat q=+\infty$ if $k\gt n$; $\lceil r\rceil$ is the smallest integer $\ge r$).
  4. For a new input, output $\mathcal C(X_{\rm test})=\{y:\ s(X_{\rm test},y)\le\hat q\}$.
Theorem — Marginal coverage of split conformal prediction (Vovk et al.; Angelopoulos & Bates, Theorem 1 and Theorems D.1–D.2)
Fix the score rule before calibration. If, conditional on training, $(X_1,Y_1),\dots,(X_n,Y_n),(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test})$ are exchangeable (i.i.d. suffices; Primer C), then $$ \mathbb P\big(Y_{\rm test}\in\mathcal C(X_{\rm test})\big)\ \ge\ 1-\alpha . $$ If in addition the scores have a continuous joint distribution (no ties almost surely), then also $$ \mathbb P\big(Y_{\rm test}\in\mathcal C(X_{\rm test})\big)\ \le\ 1-\alpha+\frac{1}{n+1}. $$ The probability is over the calibration data and the test point jointly (marginal coverage).
Proof — The rank argument (both bounds)

Let $s_i=s(X_i,Y_i)$ for the calibration points and $s_{\rm test}=s(X_{\rm test},Y_{\rm test})$. Assume the $n+1$ scores are almost surely distinct (the general case needs a tie-breaking convention). Sort the calibration scores, $s_{(1)}\lt\dots\lt s_{(n)}$, and let $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil$.

Step 1 (rewrite the event). By definition of $\mathcal C$, $\{Y_{\rm test}\in\mathcal C(X_{\rm test})\}=\{s_{\rm test}\le\hat q\}$. If $k\gt n$ then $\hat q=\infty$ and coverage is trivially $1$, so assume $k\le n$, i.e. $\alpha\ge\tfrac1{n+1}$; then $\hat q=s_{(k)}$ and the event is $\{s_{\rm test}\le s_{(k)}\}$.

Step 2 (exchangeability fixes the rank distribution). Among the $n+1$ exchangeable, a.s. distinct scores $s_1,\dots,s_n,s_{\rm test}$, the rank of $s_{\rm test}$ is uniform on $\{1,\dots,n+1\}$: any permutation of the scores has the same joint law, so no position is more likely than another. Now $s_{\rm test}\le s_{(k)}$ (the $k$-th smallest of the calibration scores) holds exactly when the rank of $s_{\rm test}$ among all $n+1$ is at most $k$ (if $s_{\rm test}$ is among the $k$ smallest of all $n+1$ points, at most $k-1$ calibration points are below it, so it lies below the $k$-th calibration order statistic, and conversely). Hence

$$ \mathbb P\big(s_{\rm test}\le s_{(k)}\big)=\frac{k}{n+1}. $$

Step 3 (both bounds). With $k=\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil$: $k\ge(n+1)(1-\alpha)$ gives $\mathbb P\ge 1-\alpha$; $k\lt(n+1)(1-\alpha)+1$ gives $\mathbb P\lt 1-\alpha+\tfrac1{n+1}$. Continuity is only needed for the upper bound (ties would push mass onto the boundary). $\square$

Where the assumptions enter. Exchangeability is used once, in Step 2, and nothing else is used: no assumption on the model, the score or the distribution. The price is that the guarantee is marginal: averaged over calibration sets and test points. Conditioning on the calibration set (Primer C), the coverage is a random variable, and its law needs more than exchangeability. If the calibration and test points are i.i.d. and the model (hence the score) was fitted on independent training data, then, conditionally on that training data, the $n+1$ scores are i.i.d. with a common CDF $F$. For continuous $F$ and $k\le n$ the conditional coverage is then $F(s_{(k)})$, the CDF evaluated at the $k$-th order statistic of $n$ i.i.d. draws, which is $\mathrm{Beta}(k,\,n+1-k)$-distributed (derivation below; for $k=n+1$ it is identically 1); writing $l=\lfloor(n+1)\alpha\rfloor$ (the largest integer $\le(n+1)\alpha$) so that $k=n+1-l$, this is the $\mathrm{Beta}(n+1-l,\ l)$ law quoted by Angelopoulos & Bates, with mean $k/(n+1)$ and standard deviation $\sqrt{kl/((n+1)^2(n+2))}\approx\sqrt{\alpha(1-\alpha)/n}$. Panel B of the explorer shows both: the mean sits inside $[1-\alpha,\,1-\alpha+\tfrac1{n+1}]$, the individual runs scatter around it.

Background — Beta distributions and uniform order statistics

For $a,b\gt0$ the $\mathrm{Beta}(a,b)$ distribution on $(0,1)$ has density proportional to $u^{a-1}(1-u)^{b-1}$, mean $a/(a+b)$ and variance $ab/[(a+b)^2(a+b+1)]$. It appears here as follows, for a fixed score function with continuous CDF $F$ and $1\le k\le n$. (i) Probability integral transform: $\mathbb P(F(s)\le u)=u$ for $u\in[0,1]$ (for strictly increasing $F$, $F(s)\le u$ iff $s\le F^{-1}(u)$, which has probability $F(F^{-1}(u))=u$; flat pieces of $F$ carry no probability), so the $U_i=F(s_i)$ are i.i.d. uniform on $[0,1]$, and because $F$ is non-decreasing, $F(s_{(k)})=U_{(k)}$, the $k$-th smallest of them. (ii) $U_{(k)}\le u$ exactly when at least $k$ of the $n$ uniforms are $\le u$, a binomial event: $\mathbb P(U_{(k)}\le u)=\sum_{j=k}^n\binom nj u^j(1-u)^{n-j}$. (iii) Differentiating, the sum telescopes to the density $\frac{n!}{(k-1)!\,(n-k)!}\,u^{k-1}(1-u)^{n-k}$, i.e. $\mathrm{Beta}(k,n+1-k)$, with mean $k/(n+1)$ and variance $k(n+1-k)/[(n+1)^2(n+2)]$. Example: $n=9$, $\alpha=0.1$ gives $k=9$, density $9u^8$, mean $0.9$ and standard deviation $0.09$, so single calibration sets scatter visibly around the marginal guarantee.

Safe planning among dynamic agents (Lindemann et al., RA-L 2023)

A robot with known dynamics $x_{t+1}=f(x_t,u_t)$ shares the space with $N$ agents whose joint trajectory $(Y_0,Y_1,\dots)\sim\mathcal D$ is unknown; a learned predictor (an LSTM in the paper; Primer E) produces forecasts $\hat Y_{\tau|t}$ of $Y_\tau$ from the observations up to time $t$. The requirement is chance-constrained (Primer C): for a constraint function $c$ that is $L$-Lipschitz in the agents’ state uniformly in the robot state, $|c(x,y)-c(x,y')|\le L\|y-y'\|$ for all $x$ (e.g. $c(x,y)=\|x-y\|-0.5$ for collision avoidance with one agent, $L=1$; with agents at positions $y^{(i)}$, $c(x,y)=\min_i\|x-y^{(i)}\|-0.5$, still with $L=1$),

$$ \mathbb P\big(c(x_t,Y_t)\ge 0\ \ \forall t\in\{0,\dots,T\}\big)\ \ge\ 1-\delta . $$

Lindemann, Cleaveland, Shim & Pappas, RA-L 2023 obtain this from split CP applied to prediction errors. Nothing in the method acts on the start: their footnote 2 assumes it is safe, $c(x_0,Y_0)\ge0$ (almost surely), and the planner below only constrains the times $1,\dots,T$. On top of that they make two assumptions: Assumption 1, the robot’s actions do not change the distribution of the agents (no interaction), and Assumption 2, a calibration set $D_{\rm cal}$ of trajectories drawn independently from $\mathcal D$.

Lemma and Theorem — Conformal prediction regions for trajectory forecasts (Lindemann et al., Lemma 1 and Theorem 1)

import Mathlib

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section
namespace SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedConformalRanks
open Set Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators Topology

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- Zero-based strict rank of an actual coordinate among all finite scores. -/
def rankNat (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores index)).card

theorem actual_rank_is_less_than_sample_size (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) :
    rankNat scores index < n := by
  have hs : Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores index) ⊂ Finset.univ := by
    refine ⟨Finset.filter_subset _ _,?_⟩
    intro hall
    have h := hall (Finset.mem_univ index)
    simp at h
  simpa [rankNat] using Finset.card_lt_card hs

def rankFin (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) : Fin n :=
  ⟨rankNat scores index,actual_rank_is_less_than_sample_size scores index⟩

theorem actual_strict_score_order_gives_strict_rank_order
    (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (first second : Fin n) (h : scores first < scores second) :
    rankNat scores first < rankNat scores second := by
  have hs : Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores first) ⊂
      Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores second) := by
    constructor
    · intro j hj
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _,
        lt_trans (Finset.mem_filter.mp hj).2 h⟩
    · intro hall
      have hi := hall (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ first,h⟩)
      simp at hi
  exact Finset.card_lt_card hs

theorem actual_distinct_scores_have_bijective_ranks (scores : Fin n → ℝ)
    (h : Function.Injective scores) : Function.Bijective (rankFin scores) := by
  have hi : Function.Injective (rankFin scores) := by
    intro i j he
    have hv : rankNat scores i=rankNat scores j := congrArg Fin.val he
    by_contra hij
    have hs : scores i ≠ scores j := fun he => hij (h he)
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hs with hs|hs
    · exact (ne_of_lt (actual_strict_score_order_gives_strict_rank_order scores i j hs)) hv
    · exact (ne_of_lt (actual_strict_score_order_gives_strict_rank_order scores j i hs)) hv.symm
  exact ⟨hi,(Finite.injective_iff_surjective).mp hi⟩

theorem actual_each_rank_occurs_exactly_once (scores : Fin n → ℝ)
    (h : Function.Injective scores) (rank : Fin n) :
    (∑ i : Fin n,if rankNat scores i=rank.val then (1:ℝ) else 0)=1 := by
  obtain ⟨index,hi⟩ := (actual_distinct_scores_have_bijective_ranks scores h).2 rank
  have he : ∀ i : Fin n,rankNat scores i=rank.val ↔ i=index := by
    intro i
    constructor
    · intro ht
      apply (actual_distinct_scores_have_bijective_ranks scores h).1
      apply Fin.ext
      exact ht.trans (congrArg Fin.val hi).symm
    · intro ht
      subst i
      exact congrArg Fin.val hi
  simp_rw [he]
  simp

theorem actual_rank_is_measurable (index : Fin n) :
    Measurable (fun scores : Fin n → ℝ => rankNat scores index) := by
  have he : (fun scores : Fin n → ℝ => rankNat scores index)=
      (fun scores => ∑ j : Fin n,if scores j<scores index then (1:ℕ) else 0) := by
    funext scores
    simp [rankNat]
  rw [he]
  exact Finset.measurable_fun_sum Finset.univ (fun j _ =>
    Measurable.ite (measurableSet_lt (measurable_pi_apply j) (measurable_pi_apply index))
      measurable_const measurable_const)

def permutedScores (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (scores : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin n → ℝ :=
  fun i => scores (permutation i)

theorem actual_permuted_scores_are_measurable (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    Measurable (permutedScores permutation) := by
  exact Measurable.of_eval (fun i => measurable_pi_apply (permutation i))

theorem actual_relabeling_preserves_the_corresponding_rank
    (permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (scores : Fin n → ℝ) (index : Fin n) :
    rankNat (permutedScores permutation scores) index=rankNat scores (permutation index) := by
  have hl : rankNat (permutedScores permutation scores) index=
      ∑ j : Fin n,if scores (permutation j)<scores (permutation index) then (1:ℕ) else 0 := by
    simp [rankNat,permutedScores]
    rfl
  rw [hl]
  calc
    _ = ∑ j : Fin n,if scores j<scores (permutation index) then (1:ℕ) else 0 :=
      Fintype.sum_equiv permutation _ _ (fun _ => rfl)
    _ = _ := by simp [rankNat]

def rankEvent (index : Fin n) (rank : Fin n) : Set (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  {scores | rankNat scores index=rank.val}

theorem actual_rank_event_measurable (index rank : Fin n) : MeasurableSet (rankEvent index rank) :=
  (actual_rank_is_measurable index) (measurableSet_singleton rank.val)

/-- Exchangeability is invariance of the genuine joint score law under every
coordinate permutation, rather than an assumed uniform-rank conclusion. -/
def exchangeable (law : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),law.map (permutedScores permutation)=law

theorem actual_exchangeability_gives_equal_coordinate_rank_probabilities
    (law : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) (h : exchangeable law) (first second rank : Fin n) :
    law.real (rankEvent first rank)=law.real (rankEvent second rank) := by
  have hm := actual_permuted_scores_are_measurable (Equiv.swap first second)
  rw [←h (Equiv.swap first second),map_measureReal_apply hm (actual_rank_event_measurable first rank)]
  have he : permutedScores (Equiv.swap first second) ⁻¹' rankEvent first rank=rankEvent second rank := by
    ext scores
    simp only [Set.mem_preimage,rankEvent,Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
    rw [actual_relabeling_preserves_the_corresponding_rank,Equiv.swap_apply_left]
  rw [he,h (Equiv.swap first second)]

theorem actual_tie_free_exchangeable_rank_is_uniform
    (law : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure law]

import Mathlib

noncomputable section
open Set MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteConformal

def strictRank {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (scores : ι → ℝ) (i : ι) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter fun j => scores j < scores i).card

def badIndices {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (scores : ι → ℝ) (rank : ℕ) : Finset ι :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun i => rank ≤ strictRank scores i

theorem strictRank_permute {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (scores : ι → ℝ) (p : Equiv.Perm ι) (i : ι) :
    strictRank (fun j => scores (p j)) i = strictRank scores (p i) := by
  classical
  unfold strictRank
  apply Finset.card_bij (fun j _ => p j)
  · intro j hj
    simpa only [Finset.mem_filter,Finset.mem_univ,true_and] using hj
  · intro a _ b _ h
    exact p.injective h
  · intro b hb
    refine ⟨p.symm b,?_,by simp⟩
    simpa only [Finset.mem_filter,Finset.mem_univ,true_and,p.apply_symm_apply] using hb

theorem badIndices_card_bound {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (scores : ι → ℝ) (rank : ℕ) :
    (badIndices scores rank).card ≤ Fintype.card ι-rank := by
  classical
  by_cases he : (badIndices scores rank).Nonempty
  · obtain ⟨i,hi,hmin⟩ := Finset.exists_min_image (badIndices scores rank) scores he
    have hk : rank ≤ strictRank scores i := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).2
    have hs : (Finset.univ.filter fun j => scores j < scores i) ⊆
        Finset.univ \ badIndices scores rank := by
      intro j hj
      refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ j,?_⟩
      intro hb
      have hji := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hj).2
      have hij := hmin j hb
      linarith
    have hc := Finset.card_le_card hs
    have heq := Finset.card_sdiff_add_card_eq_card
      (Finset.subset_univ (badIndices scores rank))
    rw [Finset.card_univ] at heq
    unfold strictRank at hk
    omega
  · have hz := Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.mp he
    simp [hz]

theorem measurable_strictRank {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (i : ι) :
    Measurable (fun scores : ι → ℝ => strictRank scores i) := by
  classical
  unfold strictRank
  simp only [Finset.card_eq_sum_ones,Finset.sum_filter]
  apply Finset.measurable_sum
  intro j _
  exact Measurable.ite (measurableSet_lt (measurable_pi_apply j) (measurable_pi_apply i))
    measurable_const measurable_const

theorem measurableSet_bad_rank {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (i : ι) (rank : ℕ) :
    MeasurableSet {scores : ι → ℝ | rank ≤ strictRank scores i} :=
  measurableSet_le measurable_const (measurable_strictRank i)

theorem exchangeable_bad_rank_equal {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype ι]
    (μ : Measure Ω) (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ)
    (hex : ∀ p : Equiv.Perm ι,
      IdentDistrib (fun ω i => scores ω (p i)) scores μ μ)
    (p : Equiv.Perm ι) (i : ι) (rank : ℕ) :
    μ {ω | rank ≤ strictRank (scores ω) (p i)} =
      μ {ω | rank ≤ strictRank (scores ω) i} := by
  have h := (hex p).measure_mem_eq (measurableSet_bad_rank i rank)
  simpa only [preimage_ofPred_eq,strictRank_permute] using h

def badEvent {Ω ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ)
    (rank : ℕ) (i : ι) : Set Ω := {ω | rank ≤ strictRank (scores ω) i}

theorem measurableSet_badEvent {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype ι]
    (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores) (rank : ℕ) (i : ι) :
    MeasurableSet (badEvent scores rank i) :=
  (measurableSet_bad_rank i rank).preimage hm

theorem bad_indicator_count {Ω ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ) (rank : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    (∑ i, (badEvent scores rank i).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ω) =
      ((badIndices (scores ω) rank).card : ℝ) := by
  classical
  simp only [badEvent,badIndices,Finset.card_eq_sum_ones,Nat.cast_sum,
    Finset.sum_filter,Nat.cast_ite,Nat.cast_one,Nat.cast_zero,Set.indicator,mem_ofPred_eq]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i _
  by_cases h : rank ≤ strictRank (scores ω) i <;> simp only [h,if_true,if_false]

theorem sum_bad_probabilities_le {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype ι]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores) (rank : ℕ) :
    (∑ i, μ.real (badEvent scores rank i)) ≤ (Fintype.card ι-rank : ℕ) := by
  classical
  have hInt : ∀ i, Integrable ((badEvent scores rank i).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))) μ :=
    fun i => (integrable_const (1 : ℝ)).indicator (measurableSet_badEvent scores hm rank i)
  have hsum : (∫ ω, ∑ i, (badEvent scores rank i).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ω ∂μ) =
      ∑ i, μ.real (badEvent scores rank i) := by
    rw [integral_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hInt i)]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    simpa only [smul_eq_mul,mul_one] using
      (integral_indicator_const (μ := μ) (1 : ℝ) (measurableSet_badEvent scores hm rank i))
  rw [← hsum]
  calc
    (∫ ω, ∑ i, (badEvent scores rank i).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ω ∂μ)
        ≤ ∫ _ω : Ω, ((Fintype.card ι-rank : ℕ) : ℝ) ∂μ := by
      apply integral_mono (integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hInt i)) (integrable_const _)
      intro ω
      change (∑ i, (badEvent scores rank i).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ω) ≤
        ((Fintype.card ι-rank : ℕ) : ℝ)
      rw [bad_indicator_count]
      exact_mod_cast badIndices_card_bound (scores ω) rank
    _ = _ := by simp

theorem exchangeable_rank_failure_bound {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores)
    (hex : ∀ p : Equiv.Perm ι,
      IdentDistrib (fun ω i => scores ω (p i)) scores μ μ)
    (rank : ℕ) (i : ι) :
    μ.real (badEvent scores rank i) ≤
      ((Fintype.card ι-rank : ℕ) : ℝ)/(Fintype.card ι : ℝ) := by
  classical
  have heach : ∀ j, μ.real (badEvent scores rank j)=μ.real (badEvent scores rank i) := by
    intro j
    have h := exchangeable_bad_rank_equal μ scores hex (Equiv.swap i j) i rank
    simpa only [Equiv.swap_apply_left,badEvent,Measure.real] using congrArg ENNReal.toReal h
  have hsum := sum_bad_probabilities_le μ scores hm rank
  simp only [heach,Finset.sum_const,Finset.card_univ,nsmul_eq_mul] at hsum
  exact (le_div_iff₀ (by exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_pos)).mpr (by simpa [mul_comm] using hsum)

/-- The kth calibration order statistic, retaining ties and adding infinity
when k exceeds the available calibration sample. The minimum of maxima of
k-element index subsets is the kth value, without deleting duplicate scores. -/
def calibrationThreshold {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (scores : ι → ℝ) (test : ι) (rank : ℕ) : EReal := by
  classical
  exact ((Finset.univ.erase test).powersetCard rank).inf
    (fun subset => subset.sup (fun j => (scores j : EReal)))

theorem calibration_failure_iff {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (scores : ι → ℝ) (test : ι) (rank : ℕ) :
    calibrationThreshold scores test rank < (scores test : EReal) ↔
      rank ≤ strictRank scores test := by
  classical
  unfold calibrationThreshold
  rw [Finset.inf_lt_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨subset,hsub,hmax⟩
    have hcard := (Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hsub).2
    have hs : subset ⊆ Finset.univ.filter (fun j => scores j < scores test) := by
      intro j hj
      refine Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ j,?_⟩
      exact EReal.coe_lt_coe_iff.mp
        (lt_of_le_of_lt (Finset.le_sup (f := fun j => (scores j : EReal)) hj) hmax)
    have hc := Finset.card_le_card hs
    simpa only [hcard,strictRank] using hc
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨subset,hsub,hcard⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq h
    refine ⟨subset,Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨?_,hcard⟩,?_⟩
    · intro j hj
      have hjlt := (Finset.mem_filter.mp (hsub hj)).2
      have hne : j ≠ test := by intro he;rw [he] at hjlt;exact (lt_irrefl _) hjlt
      exact Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hne,Finset.mem_univ j⟩
    · apply (Finset.sup_lt_iff (EReal.bot_lt_coe _)).mpr
      intro j hj
      exact EReal.coe_lt_coe_iff.mpr ((Finset.mem_filter.mp (hsub hj)).2)

theorem unavailable_calibration_rank {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (scores : ι → ℝ) (test : ι) (rank : ℕ) (h : Fintype.card ι-1 < rank) :
    calibrationThreshold scores test rank = ⊤ := by
  classical
  unfold calibrationThreshold
  have he : (Finset.univ.erase test).powersetCard rank=∅ := by
    rw [Finset.powersetCard_eq_empty,Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ test),Finset.card_univ]
    exact h
  rw [he,Finset.inf_empty]

theorem conformal_failure_bound {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores)
    (hex : ∀ p : Equiv.Perm ι,
      IdentDistrib (fun ω i => scores ω (p i)) scores μ μ)
    (rank : ℕ) (test : ι) :
    μ.real {ω | calibrationThreshold (scores ω) test rank < (scores ω test : EReal)} ≤
      ((Fintype.card ι-rank : ℕ) : ℝ)/(Fintype.card ι : ℝ) := by
  have he : {ω | calibrationThreshold (scores ω) test rank < (scores ω test : EReal)} =
      badEvent scores rank test := by
    ext ω
    exact calibration_failure_iff (scores ω) test rank
  rw [he]
  exact exchangeable_rank_failure_bound μ scores hm hex rank test

theorem conformal_success_bound {Ω ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (scores : Ω → ι → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores)
    (hex : ∀ p : Equiv.Perm ι,
      IdentDistrib (fun ω i => scores ω (p i)) scores μ μ)
    (rank : ℕ) (test : ι) :
    1-((Fintype.card ι-rank : ℕ) : ℝ)/(Fintype.card ι : ℝ) ≤
      μ.real {ω | (scores ω test : EReal) ≤ calibrationThreshold (scores ω) test rank} := by
  have he : {ω | (scores ω test : EReal) ≤ calibrationThreshold (scores ω) test rank} =
      (badEvent scores rank test)ᶜ := by
    ext ω
    simp only [mem_ofPred_eq,mem_compl_iff,badEvent]
    rw [← calibration_failure_iff]
    exact not_lt.symm
  rw [he,probReal_compl_eq_one_sub (measurableSet_badEvent scores hm rank test)]
  linarith [exchangeable_rank_failure_bound μ scores hm hex rank test]

def conformalRank (sampleCount : ℕ) (alpha : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.ceil (((sampleCount+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)*(1-alpha))

theorem conformalRank_le (n : ℕ) (alpha : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ alpha) :
    conformalRank n alpha ≤ n+1 := by
  unfold conformalRank
  apply Nat.ceil_le.mpr
  have hn : (0 : ℝ) ≤ n+1 := by positivity
  push_cast
  nlinarith

theorem conformalRank_coverage_arithmetic (n : ℕ) (alpha : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ alpha) :
    1-alpha ≤ 1-(((n+1-conformalRank n alpha : ℕ) : ℝ)/((n+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) := by
  have hle := conformalRank_le n alpha ha
  have hceil := Nat.le_ceil (((n+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)*(1-alpha))
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < ((n+1 : ℕ) : ℝ) := by positivity
  rw [Nat.cast_sub hle]
  apply sub_le_sub_left
  apply (div_le_iff₀ hpos).mpr
  change ((n+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)-conformalRank n alpha ≤ alpha*((n+1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  unfold conformalRank
  nlinarith

theorem split_conformal_coverage {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (n : ℕ) (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (scores : Ω → Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores)
    (hex : ∀ p : Equiv.Perm (Fin (n+1)),
      IdentDistrib (fun ω i => scores ω (p i)) scores μ μ)
    (alpha : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ alpha) (test : Fin (n+1)) :
    1-alpha ≤ μ.real {ω | (scores ω test : EReal) ≤
      calibrationThreshold (scores ω) test (conformalRank n alpha)} := by
  have h := conformal_success_bound μ scores hm hex (conformalRank n alpha) test
  simp only [Fintype.card_fin] at h
  exact (conformalRank_coverage_arithmetic n alpha ha).trans h

theorem rank_nineteen_ten_percent : conformalRank 19 (1/10) = 18 := by
  norm_num [conformalRank,Nat.ceil_eq_iff]

theorem rank_nineteen_one_percent : conformalRank 19 (1/100) = 20 := by
  norm_num [conformalRank,Nat.ceil_eq_iff]

theorem nineteen_calibration_coverage {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (scores : Ω → Fin 20 → ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores)
    (hex : ∀ p : Equiv.Perm (Fin 20),
      IdentDistrib (fun ω i => scores ω (p i)) scores μ μ) (test : Fin 20) :
    (9/10 : ℝ) ≤ μ.real {ω | (scores ω test : EReal) ≤
      calibrationThreshold (scores ω) test 18} := by
  have h := split_conformal_coverage 19 μ scores hm hex (1/10) (by norm_num) test
  norm_num only [rank_nineteen_ten_percent] at h
  exact h

theorem nineteen_one_percent_infinite (scores : Fin 20 → ℝ) (test : Fin 20) :
    calibrationThreshold scores test (conformalRank 19 (1/100)) = ⊤ := by
  rw [rank_nineteen_one_percent]
  exact unavailable_calibration_rank scores test 20 (by simp)

end SafeLearning.CompleteConformal

  · have hs : firstEight ∈ (Finset.univ.erase (9 : Fin 10)).powersetCard 8 := by
      apply Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr

theorem actual_sorted_scores_and_interval_endpoints :

theorem actual_nine_score_marginal_coverage_retains_whole_exchangeability

    (scores : Ω→Fin 40→Fin 4→ℝ) (hm : Measurable scores)

import SafeLearning.CompleteModulesValues
import SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsGraphViability

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section
open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped Classical

/-!
TMP future27 draft, not compiled or selected.
The grid follows viability.html's ROWS=5/COLS=8/CLIFF=4,
ACTS=[Up,Down,Left,Right,Stay], source-cell slope slide, and zero-slip semantics.
All cliff coordinates are collapsed to the one failure event, followed by
an explicit zero-reward sink. No candidate return is a hypothesis.
-/
namespace SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedExplorerSlope27

inductive Action where
  | up | down | left | right | stay
  deriving DecidableEq

inductive State where
  | live (row : Fin 4) (col : Fin 8)
  | failure | sink
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The exact six source-cell slope locations. -/
def slope (row col : ℕ) : Bool :=
  (row == 3 && decide (2 ≤ col ∧ col ≤ 5)) || (row == 2 && (col == 3 || col == 4))

/-- Nat subtraction implements JS's lower clamp for the Up/Left actions. -/
def movedRow (row : ℕ) : Action → ℕ
  | .up => row - 1
  | .down => min 4 (row + 1)
  | _ => row

def movedCol (col : ℕ) : Action → ℕ
  | .left => col - 1
  | .right => min 7 (col + 1)
  | _ => col

def cell (row col : ℕ) : State :=
  .live ⟨min 3 row, by omega⟩ ⟨min 7 col, by omega⟩

def step : State → Action → State
  | .failure, _ => .sink
  | .sink, _ => .sink
  | .live row col, a =>
      let row' := if slope row.val col.val then min 4 (movedRow row.val a + 1)
                    else movedRow row.val a
      let col' := movedCol col.val a
      if row' = 4 then .failure else cell row' col'

def available : State → Action → Prop
  | .live row col, a => slope row.val col.val = false ∨ a ≠ .up
  | _, _ => True

def upper : State := cell 2 3

def lowerLeft : State := cell 3 2

def lowerCenter : State := cell 3 3

def lowerRight : State := cell 3 4

/-- The literal reward function, including zero reward at failure and sink. -/
def reward (cost goalReward : ℝ) : State → ℝ
  | .live row col => if row.val = 3 ∧ col.val = 7 then goalReward else -cost
  | _ => 0

def failureCharge : State → ℝ
  | .failure => 1
  | _ => 0

/-- The post-failure sink is bookkeeping, excluded from the physical world. -/
def world : Set State := {s | s ≠ .sink}

def safeStates : Set State := {s | match s with
  | .live _ _ => True
  | _ => False}

def kernelStates : Set State := {s | match s with
  | .live row col => slope row.val col.val = false
  | _ => False}

def unviableStates : Set State := world \ kernelStates

theorem actual_nonslope_stay_is_safe_self_loop (row : Fin 4) (col : Fin 8)
    (hs : slope row.val col.val = false) :
    step (.live row col) .stay = .live row col := by
  have hr : row.val ≤ 3 := by omega
  have hc : col.val ≤ 7 := by omega
  have hr4 : row.val ≠ 4 := by omega
  simp [step, hs, movedRow, movedCol, cell, hr4,
    Nat.min_eq_right hr, Nat.min_eq_right hc]

set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
theorem actual_grid_kernel_is_greatest_control_invariant :
    IsGreatest {Y : Set State | Y ⊆ safeStates ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre step available Y} kernelStates := by
  refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro s hs
    cases s <;> simp_all [safeStates, kernelStates]
  · intro s hs
    cases s with
    | live row col =>
      exact ⟨.stay, by simp [available], by
        rw [actual_nonslope_stay_is_safe_self_loop row col hs]
        exact hs⟩
    | failure => simp [kernelStates] at hs
    | sink => simp [kernelStates] at hs
  · rintro Y ⟨hYs, hY⟩ s hs
    cases s with
    | live row col =>
      change slope row.val col.val = false
      by_contra hnonslope
      obtain ⟨a, ha, hnext⟩ := hY hs
      obtain ⟨b, hb, hnext2⟩ := hY hnext
      have hsafe1 := hYs hnext
      have hsafe2 := hYs hnext2
      clear hY hYs
      fin_cases row <;> fin_cases col <;>
        simp [slope] at hnonslope <;> cases a <;> cases b <;>
        simp_all [safeStates, kernelStates, available, step, cell,
          slope, movedRow, movedCol]
    | failure => simpa [safeStates, kernelStates] using hYs hs
    | sink => simpa [safeStates, kernelStates] using hYs hs

theorem actual_grid_kernel_is_exact_all_time_viability (initial : State) :
    initial ∈ kernelStates ↔ ∃ states : ℕ → State, ∃ actions : ℕ → Action,
      states 0 = initial ∧ ∀ n, states n ∈ safeStates ∧
        available (states n) (actions n) ∧ states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n) := by
  exact CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.actual_greatest_control_invariant_set_is_the_true_all_time_viability_kernel
    step available safeStates kernelStates actual_grid_kernel_is_greatest_control_invariant initial

theorem actual_unviable_reward_is_nonpositive (cost goalReward : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ cost)
    (s : State) (hs : s ∈ unviableStates) : reward cost goalReward s ≤ 0 := by
  cases s with
  | live row col =>
    by_cases hg : row.val = 3 ∧ col.val = 7
    · have hk : State.live row col ∈ kernelStates := by
        simp [kernelStates, slope, hg.1, hg.2]
      exact False.elim (hs.2 hk)
    · simpa [reward, hg] using neg_nonpos.mpr hc
  | failure => simp [reward]
  | sink => simp [reward]

theorem actual_unviable_reward_supremum_is_zero (cost goalReward : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ cost) :
    sSup (reward cost goalReward '' unviableStates) = 0 := by
  apply IsGreatest.csSup_eq
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · exact ⟨.failure, by simp [unviableStates, world, kernelStates], by simp [reward]⟩
  · rintro _ ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩
    exact actual_unviable_reward_is_nonpositive _ _ hc s hs

theorem actual_unviable_state_action_reward_supremum_is_zero
    (cost goalReward : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ cost) :
    sSup (Set.range (fun q : unviableStates × Action => reward cost goalReward q.1.val)) = 0 := by
  have he : Set.range (fun q : unviableStates × Action => reward cost goalReward q.1.val) =
      reward cost goalReward '' unviableStates := by
    ext v
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨⟨state, hs⟩, action⟩, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨state, hs, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨state, hs, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨(⟨state, hs⟩, .down), rfl⟩
  rw [he]
  exact actual_unviable_reward_supremum_is_zero cost goalReward hc

def discountedReward (discount cost goalReward : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State) : ℝ :=
  ∑' n, discount ^ n * reward cost goalReward (states n)

def discountedRisk (discount : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State) : ℝ :=
  ∑' n, discount ^ n * failureCharge (states n)

def penalizedReturn (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State) : ℝ :=
  discountedReward discount cost goalReward states - penalty * discountedRisk discount states

/-- Every realized admissible control path, not an asserted list of candidate rewards. -/
def Realizes (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action) : Prop :=
  states 0 = upper ∧
  (∀ n, available (states n) (actions n)) ∧
  ∀ n, states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n)

theorem actual_upper_available_iff (a : Action) : available upper a ↔ a ≠ .up := by
  simp [available, upper, cell, slope]

theorem actual_upper_successor_table :
    step upper .down = .failure ∧ step upper .left = lowerLeft ∧
    step upper .right = lowerRight ∧ step upper .stay = lowerCenter := by
  norm_num [step, upper, lowerLeft, lowerRight, lowerCenter, cell, slope,
    movedRow, movedCol]

theorem actual_every_lower_action_falls (s : State) (a : Action)
    (hs : s = lowerLeft ∨ s = lowerCenter ∨ s = lowerRight)
    (ha : available s a) : step s a = .failure := by
  rcases hs with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    cases a <;>
    simp_all [available, step, lowerLeft, lowerCenter, lowerRight,
      cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol]

theorem actual_sink_tail (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action) (start : ℕ)
    (hs : states start = .sink)
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n)) :
    ∀ n, start ≤ n → states n = .sink := by
  have htail : ∀ d, states (start + d) = .sink := by
    intro d
    induction d with
    | zero => simpa using hs
    | succ d ih =>
        rw [show start + (d + 1) = (start + d) + 1 by omega, hstep, ih]
        rfl
  intro n hn
  have he : n = start + (n - start) := by omega
  rw [he]
  exact htail _

set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
theorem actual_every_unviable_grid_path_fails_by_two
    (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action)
    (hzero : states 0 ∈ unviableStates)
    (hlegal : ∀ n, available (states n) (actions n))
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n)) :
    ∃ failure ≤ 2, states failure = .failure ∧
      ∀ n, failure < n → states n = .sink := by
  by_cases h0 : states 0 = .failure
  · refine ⟨0, by omega, h0, ?_⟩
    have hsink : states 1 = .sink := by simpa [h0, step] using hstep 0
    intro n hn
    exact actual_sink_tail states actions 1 hsink hstep n (by omega)
  · have hearly : states 1 = .failure ∨ states 2 = .failure := by
      have h1 := hstep 0
      have h2 := hstep 1
      have ha := hlegal 0
      have hb := hlegal 1
      cases hs : states 0 with
      | failure => exact False.elim (h0 hs)
      | sink => simp [hs, unviableStates, world] at hzero
      | live row col =>
        clear hstep hlegal
        fin_cases row <;> fin_cases col <;>
          simp [hs, unviableStates, world, kernelStates, slope] at hzero <;>
          cases ha0 : actions 0 <;> cases ha1 : actions 1 <;>
          simp_all [unviableStates, world, kernelStates, available,
            step, cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol]
    rcases hearly with h1 | h2
    · refine ⟨1, by omega, h1, ?_⟩
      have hsink : states 2 = .sink := by simpa [h1, step] using hstep 1
      intro n hn
      exact actual_sink_tail states actions 2 hsink hstep n (by omega)
    · refine ⟨2, by omega, h2, ?_⟩
      have hsink : states 3 = .sink := by simpa [h2, step] using hstep 2
      intro n hn
      exact actual_sink_tail states actions 3 hsink hstep n (by omega)

/-- The literal transition to the sink makes the failure event one-time. -/
theorem actual_grid_failure_is_visited_at_exactly_one_time
    (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action) (failure : ℕ)
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n))
    (hhit : states failure = .failure) :
    ∀ n, states n = .failure ↔ n = failure := by
  have hsink : states (failure + 1) = .sink := by
    rw [hstep, hhit]
    rfl
  have htail := actual_sink_tail states actions (failure + 1) hsink hstep
  intro n
  constructor
  · intro hnfail
    by_contra hn
    by_cases hlt : n < failure
    · have hnsink : states (n + 1) = .sink := by rw [hstep, hnfail]; rfl
      have htf := actual_sink_tail states actions (n + 1) hnsink hstep failure (by omega)
      rw [hhit] at htf
      contradiction
    · have hnsink := htail n (by omega)
      rw [hnfail] at hnsink
      contradiction
  · rintro rfl
    exact hhit

theorem actual_every_upper_path_has_the_two_failure_patterns
    (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action) (h : Realizes states actions) :
    (actions 0 = .down ∧ states 1 = .failure ∧ ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → states n = .sink) ∨
    (actions 0 ≠ .down ∧
      (states 1 = lowerLeft ∨ states 1 = lowerCenter ∨ states 1 = lowerRight) ∧
      states 2 = .failure ∧ ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → states n = .sink) := by
  rcases h with ⟨hzero, hlegal, hstep⟩
  have hfirst : states 1 = step upper (actions 0) := by simpa [hzero] using hstep 0
  have haction : actions 0 ≠ .up :=
    (actual_upper_available_iff _).mp (by simpa [hzero] using hlegal 0)
  by_cases hd : actions 0 = .down
  · left
    have hfailure : states 1 = .failure := by
      rw [hfirst, hd, actual_upper_successor_table.1]
    have hsink : states 2 = .sink := by
      simpa [hfailure, step] using hstep 1
    exact ⟨hd, hfailure, actual_sink_tail states actions 2 hsink hstep⟩
  · right
    have hlower : states 1 = lowerLeft ∨ states 1 = lowerCenter ∨ states 1 = lowerRight := by
      rw [hfirst]
      cases he : actions 0 <;>
        simp_all [step, upper, lowerLeft, lowerCenter, lowerRight,
          cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol]
    have hfailure : states 2 = .failure := by
      rw [hstep 1]
      exact actual_every_lower_action_falls _ _ hlower (hlegal 1)
    have hsink : states 3 = .sink := by
      simpa [hfailure, step] using hstep 2
    exact ⟨hd, hlower, hfailure, actual_sink_tail states actions 3 hsink hstep⟩

/-- Both infinite sums are genuine finite-support sums of the actual states. -/
theorem actual_three_term_counting_sums
    (discount cost goalReward : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State)
    (htail : ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → states n = .sink) :
    discountedReward discount cost goalReward states =
      reward cost goalReward (states 0) + discount * reward cost goalReward (states 1) +
        discount ^ 2 * reward cost goalReward (states 2) ∧
    discountedRisk discount states =
      failureCharge (states 0) + discount * failureCharge (states 1) +
        discount ^ 2 * failureCharge (states 2) := by
  constructor
  · rw [discountedReward, tsum_eq_sum (s := Finset.range 3)]
    · norm_num [Finset.sum_range_succ]
    · intro n hn
      have hn3 : 3 ≤ n := by simpa only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] using hn
      simp [htail n hn3, reward]
  · rw [discountedRisk, tsum_eq_sum (s := Finset.range 3)]
    · norm_num [Finset.sum_range_succ]
    · intro n hn
      have hn3 : 3 ≤ n := by simpa only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] using hn
      simp [htail n hn3, failureCharge]

theorem actual_every_upper_path_return_is_fast_or_slow
    (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action)
    (h : Realizes states actions) :
    penalizedReturn discount cost goalReward penalty states = -cost - discount * penalty ∨
    penalizedReturn discount cost goalReward penalty states =
      -cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty := by
  have hzero := h.1
  rcases actual_every_upper_path_has_the_two_failure_patterns states actions h with
    ⟨_, hfailure, htail⟩ | ⟨_, hlower, hfailure, htail⟩
  · left
    have hsink : states 2 = .sink := htail 2 (by omega)
    have hsums := actual_three_term_counting_sums discount cost goalReward states
      (fun n hn => htail n (by omega))
    rw [penalizedReturn, hsums.1, hsums.2, hzero, hfailure, hsink]
    norm_num [reward, failureCharge, upper, cell] <;> ring
  · right
    have hsums := actual_three_term_counting_sums discount cost goalReward states htail
    rw [penalizedReturn, hsums.1, hsums.2, hzero, hfailure]
    rcases hlower with hleft | hcenter | hright <;>
      simp_all [reward, failureCharge,
        upper, lowerLeft, lowerCenter, lowerRight, cell] <;> ring

structure Feedback where
  choose : State → Action
  legal : ∀ s, available s (choose s)

def feedbackStates (controller : Feedback) : ℕ → State
  | 0 => upper
  | n + 1 => step (feedbackStates controller n) (controller.choose (feedbackStates controller n))

def feedbackActions (controller : Feedback) (n : ℕ) : Action :=
  controller.choose (feedbackStates controller n)

def downFeedback : Feedback :=
  ⟨fun _ => .down, by intro s; cases s <;> simp [available]⟩

def stayFeedback : Feedback :=
  ⟨fun _ => .stay, by intro s; cases s <;> simp [available]⟩

def controllerReturn (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) (controller : Feedback) : ℝ :=
  penalizedReturn discount cost goalReward penalty (feedbackStates controller)

def actualUpperValue (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (Set.range (controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty))

theorem actual_every_feedback_realizes_its_path (controller : Feedback) :
    Realizes (feedbackStates controller) (feedbackActions controller) := by
  exact ⟨rfl, fun n => controller.legal _, fun _ => rfl⟩

theorem actual_down_feedback_attains_fast (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) :
    controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty downFeedback = -cost - discount * penalty := by
  have hsink : ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → feedbackStates downFeedback n = .sink :=
    actual_sink_tail _ _ 2 (by
      norm_num [feedbackStates, downFeedback, step, upper, cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol])
      (actual_every_feedback_realizes_its_path downFeedback).2.2
  have hsums := actual_three_term_counting_sums discount cost goalReward (feedbackStates downFeedback)
    (fun n hn => hsink n (by omega))
  rw [controllerReturn, penalizedReturn, hsums.1, hsums.2]
  norm_num [feedbackStates, downFeedback, reward, failureCharge, step,
    upper, cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol] <;> ring

theorem actual_stay_feedback_attains_slow (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) :
    controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty stayFeedback =
      -cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty := by
  have hsink : ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → feedbackStates stayFeedback n = .sink :=
    actual_sink_tail _ _ 3 (by
      norm_num [feedbackStates, stayFeedback, step, upper, cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol])
      (actual_every_feedback_realizes_its_path stayFeedback).2.2
  have hsums := actual_three_term_counting_sums discount cost goalReward (feedbackStates stayFeedback) hsink
  rw [controllerReturn, penalizedReturn, hsums.1, hsums.2]
  norm_num [feedbackStates, stayFeedback, reward, failureCharge, step,
    upper, cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol]
  ring

theorem actual_controller_return_set_is_exactly_the_two_source_values
    (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) :
    Set.range (controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty) =
      {-cost - discount * penalty, -cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty} := by
  ext v
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨controller, rfl⟩
    have hv := actual_every_upper_path_return_is_fast_or_slow discount cost goalReward penalty
      (feedbackStates controller) (feedbackActions controller)
      (actual_every_feedback_realizes_its_path controller)
    simpa [controllerReturn, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] using hv
  · intro hv
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hv
    rcases hv with rfl | rfl
    · exact ⟨downFeedback, actual_down_feedback_attains_fast _ _ _ _⟩
    · exact ⟨stayFeedback, actual_stay_feedback_attains_slow _ _ _ _⟩

theorem actual_controller_supremum_is_attained_source_max
    (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) :
    actualUpperValue discount cost goalReward penalty =
      max (-cost - discount * penalty) (-cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty) := by
  unfold actualUpperValue
  rw [actual_controller_return_set_is_exactly_the_two_source_values]
  exact csSup_pair _ _

theorem actual_stopped_reward_and_negative_bound_difference (discount cost penalty : ℝ) :
    (-cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty) -
      (-cost * (1 + discount + discount ^ 2) - penalty * discount ^ 2) = discount ^ 2 * cost ∧
    -cost + discount * (-cost - discount * penalty) =
      -cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty := by
  constructor <;> ring

theorem actual_slope_value_has_the_source_bound (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount ≤ 1) (hc : 0 ≤ cost) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty) :
    actualUpperValue discount cost goalReward penalty ≤ -penalty * discount ^ 2 := by
  rw [actual_controller_supremum_is_attained_source_max]
  exact CompleteModulesValues.two_step_slope_bound _ _ _ hd hd1 hc hp

theorem actual_slow_fall_strictly_wins_exactly_when_printed
    (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) (hd : 0 < discount) :
    controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty downFeedback <
      controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty stayFeedback ↔ cost < penalty * (1 - discount) := by
  rw [actual_down_feedback_attains_fast, actual_stay_feedback_attains_slow]
  exact CompleteModulesValues.slow_slope_strictly_better _ _ _ hd

theorem actual_nonnegative_reward_constant (cost : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ cost) :
    max 0 (-cost) = 0 := by simp [max_eq_left (by linarith : -cost ≤ 0)]

theorem actual_negative_reward_bound_is_below_the_value
    (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) (hd : 0 < discount) (hc : 0 < cost) :
    -cost * (1 + discount + discount ^ 2) - penalty * discount ^ 2 <
      actualUpperValue discount cost goalReward penalty := by
  rw [actual_controller_supremum_is_attained_source_max]
  exact lt_of_lt_of_le (CompleteModulesValues.negative_reward_slope_bound_false _ _ _ hd hc)
    (le_max_right _ _)

/-- A stopped sequence has the counting-measure reward exactly as printed. -/
theorem stopped_discounted_reward_is_finite_prefix (discount : ℝ) (rewards : ℕ → ℝ)
    (failure : ℕ) (hz : ∀ n, failure < n → rewards n = 0) :
    (∑' n, discount ^ n * rewards n) =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (failure + 1), discount ^ n * rewards n := by
  apply tsum_eq_sum
  intro n hn
  have hnf : failure < n := by
    have hn' : ¬n < failure + 1 := by simpa only [Finset.mem_range] using hn
    omega
  simp [hz n hnf]

/-- Finite support derives integrability, rather than making it an assumption. -/
theorem actual_finite_support_counting_integral_is_its_sum
    (terms : ℕ → ℝ) (length : ℕ) (hz : ∀ n, length ≤ n → terms n = 0) :
    Integrable terms Measure.count ∧
      (∫ n : ℕ, terms n ∂Measure.count) = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range length, terms n := by
  have hvanish (n : ℕ) (hn : n ∉ Finset.range length) : terms n = 0 := by
    apply hz n
    simpa only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] using hn
  have hnorm : Summable (fun n => ‖terms n‖) :=
    summable_of_ne_finset_zero (s := Finset.range length) (by
      intro n hn
      simp [hvanish n hn])
  have hi : Integrable terms Measure.count := integrable_count_iff.mpr hnorm
  refine ⟨hi, ?_⟩
  rw [integral_countable hi]
  simp only [count_real_singleton, one_smul]
  exact tsum_eq_sum hvanish

theorem actual_stopped_counting_integral_is_the_printed_finite_reward_sum
    (discount : ℝ) (rewards : ℕ → ℝ) (failure : ℕ)
    (hz : ∀ n, failure < n → rewards n = 0) :
    Integrable (fun n => discount ^ n * rewards n) Measure.count ∧
      (∫ n : ℕ, discount ^ n * rewards n ∂Measure.count) =
        ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (failure + 1), discount ^ n * rewards n := by
  apply actual_finite_support_counting_integral_is_its_sum
  intro n hn
  simp [hz n (by omega)]

theorem single_failure_discounted_risk_is_arrival_weight (discount : ℝ) (failure : ℕ) :
    (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) = discount ^ failure := by
  rw [tsum_eq_single failure]
  · simp
  · intro n hn
    simp [hn]

theorem actual_single_failure_counting_integral_is_arrival_weight
    (discount : ℝ) (failure : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun n : ℕ => discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) Measure.count ∧
      (∫ n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ) ∂Measure.count) =
        discount ^ failure := by
  have hvanish : ∀ n : ℕ, failure + 1 ≤ n →
      discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ) = 0 := by
    intro n hn
    simp [show n ≠ failure by omega]
  have hi := actual_finite_support_counting_integral_is_its_sum
    (fun n : ℕ => discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) (failure + 1) hvanish
  refine ⟨hi.1, ?_⟩
  rw [integral_countable hi.1]
  simp only [count_real_singleton, one_smul]
  exact single_failure_discounted_risk_is_arrival_weight _ _

/-- No one-time-charge or vanishing-tail assumption is needed for this actual grid path. -/
theorem actual_grid_arrival_derives_the_counting_reward_and_risk
    (discount cost goalReward : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action)
    (failure : ℕ) (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n))
    (hhit : states failure = .failure) :
    discountedReward discount cost goalReward states =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (failure + 1), discount ^ n * reward cost goalReward (states n) ∧
    discountedRisk discount states = discount ^ failure := by
  have hsink : states (failure + 1) = .sink := by rw [hstep, hhit]; rfl
  have htail := actual_sink_tail states actions (failure + 1) hsink hstep
  have honce := actual_grid_failure_is_visited_at_exactly_one_time states actions failure hstep hhit
  constructor
  · apply stopped_discounted_reward_is_finite_prefix
    intro n hn
    simp [htail n (by omega), reward]
  · unfold discountedRisk
    have hcharge (n : ℕ) : failureCharge (states n) = (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ) := by
      by_cases hn : n = failure
      · subst n
        simp [hhit, failureCharge]
      · have hnf : states n ≠ .failure := fun h => hn ((honce n).mp h)
        cases he : states n <;> simp_all [failureCharge]
    simp_rw [hcharge]
    exact single_failure_discounted_risk_is_arrival_weight discount failure

theorem nonnegative_reward_bound_allows_horizon_extension
    (discount bound : ℝ) (failure horizon : ℕ) (hd : 0 ≤ discount)
    (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (ht : failure ≤ horizon) :
    bound * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (failure + 1), discount ^ n) ≤
      bound * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (horizon + 1), discount ^ n) := by
  apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ hb
  exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg
    (Finset.range_mono (by omega)) (by intros; positivity)

theorem negative_reward_bound_reverses_horizon_extension
    (discount bound : ℝ) (failure horizon : ℕ) (hd : 0 ≤ discount)
    (hb : bound ≤ 0) (ht : failure ≤ horizon) :
    bound * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (horizon + 1), discount ^ n) ≤
      bound * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (failure + 1), discount ^ n) := by
  apply mul_le_mul_of_nonpos_left _ hb
  exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg
    (Finset.range_mono (by omega)) (by intros; positivity)

theorem counting_sum_doomed_return_bound (discount bound penalty : ℝ)
    (rewards : ℕ → ℝ) (failure horizon : ℕ) (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1)
    (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty) (ht : failure ≤ horizon)
    (hr : ∀ n < failure + 1, rewards n ≤ bound)
    (hz : ∀ n, failure < n → rewards n = 0) :
    (∑' n, discount ^ n * rewards n) -
      penalty * (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) ≤
      bound * (1 - discount ^ (horizon + 1)) / (1 - discount) - penalty * discount ^ horizon := by
  rw [stopped_discounted_reward_is_finite_prefix discount rewards failure hz,
    single_failure_discounted_risk_is_arrival_weight]
  exact CompleteModulesValues.finite_discounted_doomed_bound _ _ _ _ _ _ hd hd1 hb hp ht hr

/-- Adding a safe predecessor of the greatest invariant set cannot enlarge it. -/
theorem actual_unviability_is_forward_invariant_before_failure
    {S A : Type*} (dynamics : S → A → S) (allowed : S → A → Prop)
    (safe kernel : Set S)
    (hk : IsGreatest {Y : Set S | Y ⊆ safe ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed Y} kernel)
    (x : S) (a : A) (hx : x ∉ kernel) (hsafe : x ∈ safe) (ha : allowed x a) :
    dynamics x a ∉ kernel := by
  intro hnext
  have hgrown : insert x kernel ⊆ safe ∧ insert x kernel ⊆
      CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed (insert x kernel) := by
    constructor
    · intro y hy
      rcases hy with rfl | hy
      · exact hsafe
      · exact hk.1.1 hy
    · intro y hy
      rcases hy with rfl | hy
      · exact ⟨a, ha, Or.inr hnext⟩
      · obtain ⟨b, hb, hsuccessor⟩ := hk.1.2 hy
        exact ⟨b, hb, Or.inr hsuccessor⟩
  exact hx (hk.2 hgrown (by simp))

theorem actual_every_visited_prefailure_state_is_unviable
    {S A : Type*} (dynamics : S → A → S) (allowed : S → A → Prop)
    (safe kernel : Set S)
    (hk : IsGreatest {Y : Set S | Y ⊆ safe ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed Y} kernel)
    (states : ℕ → S) (actions : ℕ → A) (failure : ℕ)
    (hzero : states 0 ∉ kernel) (hsafe : ∀ n < failure, states n ∈ safe)
    (hallowed : ∀ n, allowed (states n) (actions n))
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = dynamics (states n) (actions n)) :
    ∀ n ≤ failure, states n ∉ kernel := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero => intro _; exact hzero
  | succ n ih =>
    intro hn
    rw [hstep n]
    exact actual_unviability_is_forward_invariant_before_failure dynamics allowed safe kernel hk
      _ _ (ih (by omega)) (hsafe n (by omega)) (hallowed n)

/-- The source's bound on X_U×U now supplies the actual visited reward bound. -/
theorem actual_unviable_trajectory_counting_sum_bound
    {S A : Type*} (dynamics : S → A → S) (allowed : S → A → Prop)
    (safe kernel failureStates : Set S)
    (hk : IsGreatest {Y : Set S | Y ⊆ safe ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed Y} kernel)
    (states : ℕ → S) (actions : ℕ → A) (r : S → A → ℝ)
    (discount bound penalty : ℝ) (failure horizon : ℕ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1) (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty)
    (ht : failure ≤ horizon) (hzero : states 0 ∉ kernel)
    (hsafe : ∀ n < failure, states n ∈ safe)
    (hallowed : ∀ n, allowed (states n) (actions n))
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = dynamics (states n) (actions n))
    (hr : ∀ x ∉ kernel, ∀ a, allowed x a → r x a ≤ bound)
    (hz : ∀ n, failure < n → r (states n) (actions n) = 0)
    (hfailure : ∀ n, states n ∈ failureStates ↔ n = failure) :
    (∑' n, discount ^ n * r (states n) (actions n)) -
      penalty * (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if states n ∈ failureStates then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) ≤
      bound * (1 - discount ^ (horizon + 1)) / (1 - discount) - penalty * discount ^ horizon := by
  have hvisited := actual_every_visited_prefailure_state_is_unviable dynamics allowed safe kernel hk
    states actions failure hzero hsafe hallowed hstep
  simp_rw [hfailure]
  apply counting_sum_doomed_return_bound _ _ _ _ _ _ hd hd1 hb hp ht
  · intro n hn
    exact hr (states n) (hvisited n (by omega)) (actions n) (hallowed n)
  · exact hz

theorem both_controller_and_state_suprema_preserve_counting_sum_bound
    {X Controller : Type*} [Nonempty X] [Nonempty Controller]
    (discount bound penalty : ℝ) (rewards : X → Controller → ℕ → ℝ)
    (failure : X → Controller → ℕ) (horizon : ℕ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1) (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty)
    (ht : ∀ x u, failure x u ≤ horizon)
    (hr : ∀ x u n, n < failure x u + 1 → rewards x u n ≤ bound)
    (hz : ∀ x u n, failure x u < n → rewards x u n = 0) :
    sSup (Set.range (fun x => sSup (Set.range (fun u =>
      (∑' n, discount ^ n * rewards x u n) - penalty *
        (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if n = failure x u then 1 else 0 : ℝ)))))) ≤
      bound * (1 - discount ^ (horizon + 1)) / (1 - discount) - penalty * discount ^ horizon := by
  apply CompleteModulesValues.supremum_doomed_bound
  · exact Set.range_nonempty _
  · intro x
    apply CompleteModulesValues.supremum_doomed_bound
    · exact Set.range_nonempty _
    · intro u
      exact counting_sum_doomed_return_bound _ _ _ _ _ _ hd hd1 hb hp (ht x u)
        (hr x u) (hz x u)

/-- This is the source supremum convention even when the unviable set is empty.
For a nonempty set it coincides with the real-valued outer supremum above. -/
theorem source_extended_outer_supremum_preserves_the_uniform_doomed_bound
    {X Controller : Type*} [Nonempty Controller]
    (discount bound penalty : ℝ) (rewards : X → Controller → ℕ → ℝ)
    (failure : X → Controller → ℕ) (horizon : ℕ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1) (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty)
    (ht : ∀ x u, failure x u ≤ horizon)
    (hr : ∀ x u n, n < failure x u + 1 → rewards x u n ≤ bound)
    (hz : ∀ x u n, failure x u < n → rewards x u n = 0) :
    sSup (Set.range (fun x => ((sSup (Set.range (fun u =>
      (∑' n, discount ^ n * rewards x u n) - penalty *
        (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if n = failure x u then 1 else 0 : ℝ)))) : ℝ) : EReal))) ≤
      ((bound * (1 - discount ^ (horizon + 1)) / (1 - discount) -
        penalty * discount ^ horizon : ℝ) : EReal) := by
  apply sSup_le
  rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
  apply EReal.coe_le_coe
  apply CompleteModulesValues.supremum_doomed_bound
  · exact Set.range_nonempty _
  · intro u
    exact counting_sum_doomed_return_bound _ _ _ _ _ _ hd hd1 hb hp (ht x u)
      (hr x u) (hz x u)

/-- The source reward supremum is over physical unviable states, not the
post-failure bookkeeping sink. Boundedness comes from the source reward scope. -/
theorem actual_reward_supremum_bounds_each_physical_unviable_state_action
    {S A : Type*} (physical kernel : Set S) (r : S → A → ℝ)
    (hbounded : BddAbove (Set.range (fun q : {s : S // s ∈ physical ∧ s ∉ kernel} × A => r q.1.val q.2)))
    (x : S) (hx : x ∈ physical) (hxk : x ∉ kernel) (a : A) :
    r x a ≤ sSup (Set.range (fun q : {s : S // s ∈ physical ∧ s ∉ kernel} × A => r q.1.val q.2)) := by
  exact le_csSup hbounded ⟨(⟨x, ⟨hx, hxk⟩⟩, a), rfl⟩

/-- Every visited reward bound is derived from the actual physical-state
supremum and the greatest-kernel property; no bound outside the world is
required. The explicit arrival and sink semantics match the source. -/
theorem source_physical_unviable_trajectory_counting_sum_bound
    {S A : Type*} (dynamics : S → A → S) (allowed : S → A → Prop)
    (physical safe kernel failureStates : Set S)
    (hk : IsGreatest {Y : Set S | Y ⊆ safe ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed Y} kernel)
    (states : ℕ → S) (actions : ℕ → A) (r : S → A → ℝ)
    (discount bound penalty : ℝ) (failure horizon : ℕ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1) (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty)
    (ht : failure ≤ horizon) (hzero : states 0 ∉ kernel)
    (hphysical : ∀ n ≤ failure, states n ∈ physical)
    (hsafe : ∀ n < failure, states n ∈ safe)
    (hallowed : ∀ n, allowed (states n) (actions n))
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = dynamics (states n) (actions n))
    (hbounded : BddAbove (Set.range (fun q : {s : S // s ∈ physical ∧ s ∉ kernel} × A => r q.1.val q.2)))
    (hsup : sSup (Set.range (fun q : {s : S // s ∈ physical ∧ s ∉ kernel} × A => r q.1.val q.2)) ≤ bound)
    (hz : ∀ n, failure < n → r (states n) (actions n) = 0)
    (hfailure : ∀ n, states n ∈ failureStates ↔ n = failure) :
    (∑' n, discount ^ n * r (states n) (actions n)) -
      penalty * (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if states n ∈ failureStates then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) ≤
      bound * (1 - discount ^ (horizon + 1)) / (1 - discount) - penalty * discount ^ horizon := by
  have hvisited := actual_every_visited_prefailure_state_is_unviable dynamics allowed safe kernel hk
    states actions failure hzero hsafe hallowed hstep
  simp_rw [hfailure]
  apply counting_sum_doomed_return_bound _ _ _ _ _ _ hd hd1 hb hp ht
  · intro n hn
    exact le_trans (actual_reward_supremum_bounds_each_physical_unviable_state_action
      physical kernel r hbounded (states n) (hphysical n (by omega))
      (hvisited n (by omega)) (actions n)) hsup
  · exact hz

/-- The source's two suprema now range over actual state/control trajectories.
An empty unviable initial-state domain has extended supremum minus infinity. -/
theorem source_actual_state_and_controller_suprema_have_the_uniform_bound
    {S A X Controller : Type*} [Nonempty Controller]
    (dynamics : S → A → S) (allowed : S → A → Prop)
    (physical safe kernel failureStates : Set S)
    (hk : IsGreatest {Y : Set S | Y ⊆ safe ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed Y} kernel)
    (states : X → Controller → ℕ → S) (actions : X → Controller → ℕ → A)
    (r : S → A → ℝ) (failure : X → Controller → ℕ)
    (discount bound penalty : ℝ) (horizon : ℕ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1) (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty)
    (ht : ∀ x u, failure x u ≤ horizon)
    (hzero : ∀ x u, states x u 0 ∉ kernel)
    (hphysical : ∀ x u n, n ≤ failure x u → states x u n ∈ physical)
    (hsafe : ∀ x u n, n < failure x u → states x u n ∈ safe)
    (hallowed : ∀ x u n, allowed (states x u n) (actions x u n))
    (hstep : ∀ x u n, states x u (n + 1) = dynamics (states x u n) (actions x u n))
    (hbounded : BddAbove (Set.range (fun q : {s : S // s ∈ physical ∧ s ∉ kernel} × A => r q.1.val q.2)))
    (hsup : sSup (Set.range (fun q : {s : S // s ∈ physical ∧ s ∉ kernel} × A => r q.1.val q.2)) ≤ bound)
    (hz : ∀ x u n, failure x u < n → r (states x u n) (actions x u n) = 0)
    (hfailure : ∀ x u n, states x u n ∈ failureStates ↔ n = failure x u) :
    sSup (Set.range (fun x => ((sSup (Set.range (fun u =>
      (∑' n, discount ^ n * r (states x u n) (actions x u n)) - penalty *
        (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if states x u n ∈ failureStates then 1 else 0 : ℝ)))) : ℝ) : EReal))) ≤
      ((bound * (1 - discount ^ (horizon + 1)) / (1 - discount) -
        penalty * discount ^ horizon : ℝ) : EReal) := by
  apply sSup_le
  rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
  apply EReal.coe_le_coe
  apply CompleteModulesValues.supremum_doomed_bound
