Connection to Module 10 — reachability values are not Lagrange values
HJ reachability also encodes $X_V$ in a value function, but one of a different type: $V_{\mathrm{BRT}}(x) = \sup_{u} \inf_{t \ge 0} \ell(\varphi^u_x(t))$ with $\ell$ a signed distance to $X_F$ (see Primer A), whose positive level certifies a safety margin; identifying its zero superlevel set with $X_V$ needs additional boundary assumptions. This is a minimum over time along the trajectory, not a discounted integral, so it is not a Lagrange-type value function and does not come with the usual RL machinery. Fisac et al., ICRA 2019 showed that its discounted version $V(s) = (1-\gamma)\ell(s) + \gamma \min\{\ell(s), \max_a V(s^+_a)\}$ is a contraction (see Primer E) and can be learned by Q-learning (see Primer E). Safe value functions, by contrast, keep the standard discounted return and ask when it already encodes the kernel.
Going deeper — the signed distance and why the zero level is delicate

Take $\ell(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,X_F)-\operatorname{dist}(x,X\setminus X_F)$, where $\operatorname{dist}(x,S)=\inf_{y\in S}\|x-y\|_2$. Thus $\ell$ is positive outside failure, negative in its interior and zero on the boundary (for a nonempty closed failure set with nonempty complement). Then $V_{\mathrm{BRT}}>0$ certifies a trajectory with a positive safety margin, and $V_{\mathrm{BRT}}<0$ rules out safety. The zero level requires additional conventions and assumptions. For example, under $\dot x=-x$ with failure $x\le0$, every $x>0$ is safe but $\inf_{t\ge0}x e^{-t}=0$; the failed state $x=0$ also has value zero. So neither $\{V_{\mathrm{BRT}}\ge0\}$ (which contains the failed state $0$) nor $\{V_{\mathrm{BRT}}\gt0\}$ (which is empty) equals $X_V=\{x\gt0\}$: identifying a level set of this infinite-horizon value with $X_V$ needs extra conventions.

Here $s_a^+=f(s,a)$ is the successor under action $a$. Let $BV$ denote the right-hand side as a function of $s$. A maximum and a minimum each change by at most the largest change in their arguments, and the term $(1-\gamma)\ell(s)$ does not depend on $V$, so $|BV(s)-BW(s)|\le\gamma\max_a|V(s_a^+)-W(s_a^+)|$ and therefore $\|BV-BW\|_\infty\le\gamma\|V-W\|_\infty$, with $\|V-W\|_\infty=\max_s|V(s)-W(s)|$ on a finite state space. This contraction property is what makes value iteration converge (and, with the usual step-size conditions, Q-learning).

Worked example — The shelf: a one-dimensional kernel with a known time-to-failure

Massiani et al. (Section VI-A) use a piecewise-affine model that we will reuse for the threshold theorem. A robot drives on a shelf of length $L$ at speed $\pm v$ or stands still: $X = [-L, L]$, $U = \{-v, 0, v\}$,

$$\dot x = \begin{cases} u(x), & x \in [0, L), \\ -L/T_f, & x \in (-L, 0), \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \qquad X_F = \{-L\}.$$

On $[0, L)$ the robot controls its motion. If it crosses the ledge at $x = 0$ it falls at constant speed $L/T_f$ and breaks on the ground at $x = -L$, where the trajectory stops. Hence $X_V = [0, L]$ (the robot can stand still anywhere on the shelf, and at the wall $x = L$ it is stuck, $\dot x = 0$) and $X_U = [-L, 0)$: the paper writes $(-L, 0)$ for the doomed but not yet failed part, and the failure state $-L$ belongs to $X_U$ as well. Every unviable trajectory reaches $X_F$ within time $T_f$, exactly the uniform time-to-failure bound that Assumption 1 in Section 4 asks for. Note the discontinuity of $f$ at $x = 0$: the fall is not a Lipschitz continuation (see Primer B) of the driving dynamics. Section 4 explains why this is not an accident.

For this toy model we use the intended event-driven trajectory convention: commanding zero at the ledge keeps the robot there, while commanding motion over the ledge initiates the constant-speed fall. This convention is part of the model. The discontinuous differential equation alone does not establish uniqueness at the ledge, so the usual Lipschitz existence-and-uniqueness result cannot be applied there.

Worked example — The hovership toy model of Heim et al.

The CoRL 2019 paper introduces its objects on a five-state grid world: a hovering spaceship pulled towards the ground by a gravity that is stronger near the ground; it can fire two levels of thrust or let itself fall. With failure set $S_F = \{5\}$ (the crash), the viability kernel is $S_V = \{1, 2, 3\}$. Two details are worth remembering. State $3$ is viable but can no longer reach the other viable states: avoiding failure does not require ergodicity (see Module 6). State $4$ is neither in $S_V$ nor in $S_F$: it has not failed yet but cannot avoid failing, the "sliding on ice" situation. Finally, from state $3$ exactly one action keeps the ship alive, which is what the safety measure of the next section quantifies as $\Lambda(3) = 1$.

2. A Learnable Safety Measure

A binary label "viable / unviable" hides how close to failure a state is. Heim, von Rohr, Trimpe & Badri-Spröwitz, CoRL 2019 propose a graded notion: count the viable actions. This section uses their notation, $s' = T(s, a)$ with $q = (s, a) \in Q = S \times A$.

Definition — Safety measure, Q-safety measure, safe level sets (Heim et al., Defs. 3–5)
The safety measure $\Lambda(s) \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is the volume of the slice of the viable set at $s$, $$\Lambda(s) = \operatorname{vol}\{a \in A : (s,a) \in Q_V\},$$ with the Lebesgue measure on continuous action spaces (assuming measurability) and the counting measure on discrete ones. The Q-safety measure transports it to state-action space through the dynamics, $\Lambda_Q(q) = \Lambda(T(q))$. For a level $\lambda \ge 0$ the safe level sets are $S_\lambda = \{s : \Lambda(s) \gt \lambda\}$ and $Q_\lambda = \{q : \Lambda_Q(q) \gt \lambda\}$. With the counting measure viability means $\Lambda(s) \gt 0$ (a viable state has at least one viable action), so the viable set is recovered as $Q_V = Q_{\lambda = 0}$. With the Lebesgue measure this needs every nonempty slice $\{a : (s,a) \in Q_V\}$ to have positive volume, which the paper assumes tacitly: a viable state whose only viable input is a single point has $\Lambda(s) = 0$.
Intuition
A high $\Lambda(s)$ means many viability-maintaining actions are available: the agent can be sloppy. A low value means the agent must be precise and deliberate, because few actions avoid failure now and in the future. Sampling from $Q_\lambda$ moves the system to a state $s'$ with $\Lambda(s') \gt \lambda$, i.e. with more than $\lambda$ viable actions to choose from, which is useful when disturbances are expected. The paper adds that the margin can then be kept indefinitely; that does not follow from the definitions alone, because a state with $\Lambda(s') \gt \lambda$ need not have any successor with $\Lambda \gt \lambda$ (two viable actions that both lead to a state with a single viable action). An indefinite margin needs the viability kernel of $S_\lambda$, computed like $X_V$ with $S_\lambda$ in place of $X \setminus X_F$. The measure implicitly encodes both the dynamics and the failure set; nothing else about the system needs to be known. Section 5 will show that maximum-entropy RL is drawn to high-$\Lambda$ states on its own.

Learning the measure from samples, and why failures are informative

The goal is a large, conservative estimate $\hat Q_V \subseteq Q_V$ (see Module 4) obtained model-free. The agent picks an action $a$ in state $s$ and receives the tuple $(s', \mathrm{failed})$. Two kinds of samples arrive: a failure is the only direct observation of the ground truth, $\Lambda_Q(q) = 0$; a success only yields the current estimate $\hat\Lambda(s')$ of the next state's measure, which is itself computed from $\hat\Lambda_Q$. The learning signal therefore flows from failures outwards.

Theorem — Tabular safety-measure convergence (Heim et al. 2019, Thm. 1)
Let $S$ and $A$ be finite and the transition map $T$ deterministic (discrete time; the setting of the paper's Appendix A, not the GP of the practical algorithm). The estimate of the viable set is $\hat Q_V=\{q:\hat\Lambda_Q(q)\gt0\}$ and the state estimate counts its slice, $\hat\Lambda(s)=\#\{a\in A:\hat\Lambda_Q(s,a)\gt0\}$. Use the tabular update $\hat\Lambda_Q(q) \leftarrow 0$ after a failure and $\hat\Lambda_Q(q) \leftarrow \hat\Lambda(s')$ otherwise. If every pair $q\in Q$ is updated infinitely often (the paper's "infinite random sampling over $Q$"; independent draws that give every pair positive probability achieve this with probability one), then $\hat\Lambda_Q$ converges to the correct value $0$ for all $q \in Q_V^c$ (the unviable and failed pairs). Once this has happened, $\hat Q_V$ is tightly bounded from above and $\hat\Lambda \le \Lambda$; if the estimate was initialised optimistically on the viable pairs, $Q_V \subseteq \hat Q_V$ (i.e. $\hat\Lambda_Q \gt 0$ on $Q_V$, implied by the pointwise $\hat\Lambda_Q \ge \Lambda_Q$), it converges to the true measure. The paper phrases the optimism state-wise, "initially $\hat\Lambda \ge \Lambda$", which is not enough (counterexample below).

Proof idea (Heim et al., CoRL 2019, App. A): from an unviable state every trajectory fails without revisiting a state, so within at most $|S|$ steps. Pairs that fail in one step are set to $0$ by their first update and stay there; after that, pairs whose successor only has such actions copy $\hat\Lambda(s')=0$, and so on backwards along every doomed chain. Exhaustive updates make each stage happen eventually. The GP algorithm below uses a probability-thresholded estimate and does not inherit this theorem.

Why the two conditions. Non-failure samples only ever copy estimates and failures only ever lower them, so a viable pair that is wrongly assigned $0$ can be repaired only through a successor state whose estimate is still positive; once the zeros close a loop they are permanent. Optimism is needed so that errors are only ever in the direction that failures can fix, and it has to hold pair by pair: the invariant $Q_V \subseteq \hat Q_V$ survives every update (a viable pair's successor $s' \in S_V$ keeps at least its $\Lambda(s') \ge 1$ viable actions positive), and together with the theorem it forces $\hat Q_V = Q_V$, hence $\hat\Lambda = \Lambda$. The state-wise $\hat\Lambda \ge \Lambda$ does not suffice: take one viable state $s$ with a safe self-loop $a_1$ and a failing action $a_2$, initialised $\hat\Lambda_Q(s,a_1) = 0$, $\hat\Lambda_Q(s,a_2) = 1$, so that $\hat\Lambda(s) = 1 = \Lambda(s)$; if $a_2$ is sampled first, $\hat\Lambda(s)$ drops to $0$ and the self-loop copies $0$ forever. Infinite sampling is what lets every unviable pair eventually be observed as a failure, directly or through the chain $\hat\Lambda_Q(q) = \hat\Lambda(T(q))$. Both are the usual conditions of model-free learning and both are impractical, since optimistic starts encourage visits to the failure set. The practical algorithm trades the guarantee for confidence bounds.

Algorithm idea — A GP over $\Lambda_Q$ with an optimistic and a cautious set
Model $\hat\Lambda_Q(q) \mid \mathcal{D} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu(q), \sigma^2(q))$ with a Gaussian process (Module 3) on $\mathcal{D} = \{(q_i, \hat\Lambda_i(s'_i))\}$ (a practical approximation: the mass below zero is read as the probability of the point being unviable). Then $P[\hat\Lambda_Q \gt \lambda \mid \mathcal{D}] \approx 1 - F_{\hat\Lambda_Q}(\lambda)$ with $F$ the normal CDF (see Primer C), and two thresholded sets drive learning: $$\begin{aligned} \hat Q_{\mathrm{opt}}(\gamma_{\mathrm{opt}}) &= \{q : P[\hat\Lambda_Q \gt 0] \gt \gamma_{\mathrm{opt}}\}, \\ \hat Q_{\mathrm{caut}}(\gamma_{\mathrm{caut}}, \lambda_{\mathrm{caut}}) &= \{q : P[\hat\Lambda_Q \gt \lambda_{\mathrm{caut}}] \gt \gamma_{\mathrm{caut}}\}. \end{aligned}$$ $\hat Q_{\mathrm{opt}}$ is used to compute $\hat\Lambda$ (optimism, needed for convergence); $\hat Q_{\mathrm{caut}}$ is used for active sampling (caution, needed to avoid failures). Choosing $\lambda_{\mathrm{caut}}\ge0$ and $\gamma_{\mathrm{caut}} \ge \gamma_{\mathrm{opt}}$ gives $\hat Q_{\mathrm{caut}} \subseteq \hat Q_{\mathrm{opt}}$, so the agent never purposefully explores outside its current estimate of the viable set. (Here $\gamma_{\mathrm{opt}}$, $\gamma_{\mathrm{caut}} \in [0,1]$ are confidence levels, not discount factors.)
Derivation — the exceedance probability and why the cautious set is inside the optimistic one

For $\sigma(q)>0$, the Gaussian-model probability is $1-\Phi((\lambda-\mu(q))/\sigma(q))$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF. This calculation is exact within the Gaussian model; its interpretation as true viability probability is approximate. Assume $\lambda_{\mathrm{caut}}\ge0$. Then the event $\{\hat\Lambda_Q>\lambda_{\mathrm{caut}}\}$ is contained in $\{\hat\Lambda_Q>0\}$, so for $q\in\hat Q_{\mathrm{caut}}$: $P[\hat\Lambda_Q(q)>0]\ge P[\hat\Lambda_Q(q)>\lambda_{\mathrm{caut}}]>\gamma_{\mathrm{caut}}\ge\gamma_{\mathrm{opt}}$, i.e. $q\in\hat Q_{\mathrm{opt}}$. (With $\lambda_{\mathrm{caut}}\lt0$ the first inclusion fails and the containment can fail.)

If $\sigma(q)=0$, the model is a point mass at $\mu(q)$ and the strict exceedance probability is $\mathbf1\{\mu(q)>\lambda\}$.

Algorithm 2: Learning the safety measure (Heim et al., Alg. 1)
  1. Input: initial GP estimate $\hat\Lambda_Q$, thresholds $\gamma_{\mathrm{caut}}, \gamma_{\mathrm{opt}}, \lambda_{\mathrm{caut}}$, initial state $s_0$, budget $n$
  2. while $i \lt n$:
  3. compute $\hat\Lambda$, $\hat Q_{\mathrm{opt}}$, $\hat Q_{\mathrm{caut}}$ from $\hat\Lambda_Q$; $A_{\mathrm{caut}} \leftarrow \{a : (s_i, a) \in \hat Q_{\mathrm{caut}}\}$
  4. if $A_{\mathrm{caut}} = \emptyset$: $a_i \leftarrow \arg\max_a P[\hat\Lambda_Q(s_i,a) \gt 0 \mid \mathcal{D}]$ // take the safest action: the most probably viable one. The paper writes $P[(s_i,a) \in \hat Q_{\mathrm{caut}}]$, which is $0$ for every $a$ once the set is thresholded; the authors' code (vibly) maximises this unthresholded probability, plus a little noise to break ties
  5. else: $a_i \leftarrow \arg\max_{a \in A_{\mathrm{caut}}} \sigma^2(s_i, a)$ // explore where the GP is most uncertain
  6. $(s_{i+1}, \mathrm{failed}) \leftarrow T(s_i, a_i)$
  7. if failed: add $((s_i, a_i), 0)$ to $\mathcal{D}$, refit, reset $s_{i+1}$ to a random state of $\hat Q_{\mathrm{caut}}$
  8. else: compute $\hat\Lambda(s_{i+1})$ from $\hat Q_{\mathrm{opt}}$, add $((s_i, a_i), \hat\Lambda(s_{i+1}))$ to $\mathcal{D}$, refit

"A random state of $\hat Q_{\mathrm{caut}}$" means a state of its projection onto the state space, $\{s:\exists a,\ (s,a)\in\hat Q_{\mathrm{caut}}\}$. The rule presupposes that this set is nonempty and that the experiment can be reset to a chosen state; otherwise an externally supplied reset state is needed.

3. Penalising Failure: The Setup

Back to control notation. The reward $r : X \times U \to \mathbb{R}$ is measurable and bounded. For a controller $u$ and initial state $x$ the return is

$$G(x,u) = \int_{\mathbb{T}} e^{-t/\tau}\, r\big(\varphi^u_x(t), \hat u_x(t)\big)\, dt, \qquad \hat u_x(t) = u(\varphi^u_x(t)),$$

with the discount time constant $\tau \gt 0$; in discrete time the integral is a sum and $e^{-t/\tau} = \gamma^t$ with $\gamma = e^{-1/\tau}$. The smaller $\tau$, the shorter the agent's inner time horizon, although large delayed rewards can still matter. Because $r$ is bounded the return is finite for every $u$ and $x$. The (unconstrained) value function is $v(x) = \sup_{u \in \mathcal{U}} G(x,u)$ and satisfies the dynamic-programming identity (see Primer D), for all $t$,

$$\begin{gathered} v(x) = \sup_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \left[ \int_0^{t} e^{-s/\tau} r\big(\varphi^u_x(s), \hat u_x(s)\big)\, ds + e^{-(t + \delta t)/\tau}\, v\big(\varphi^u_x(t + \delta t)\big) \right], \\ \delta t = \begin{cases} 1 & \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{N} \\ 0 & \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}_+ \end{cases} \end{gathered}$$

The $\delta t$ bookkeeping is what produces the extra term in the discrete-time theorems. In discrete time the integral up to $t$ is the sum $\sum_{k=0}^{t}\gamma^k r(x_k,u_k)$, which already contains the reward at step $t$, so the "rest of the trajectory" starts one step later, at $x_{t+1}$, with weight $\gamma^{t+1}$; in continuous time the split point itself carries no reward and the continuation starts at $t$.

Lemma — The discounted risk (Massiani et al., Lemma 1)
For $x \in X$ and $u \in \mathcal{U}$ define $$\rho(x,u) = \int_{\mathbb{T}} e^{-t/\tau}\, \delta_{X_F}\big(\varphi^u_x(t)\big)\, dt,$$ where $\delta_{X_F}$ is the indicator function of $X_F$ in discrete time and, in the paper's words, "the Dirac distribution" in continuous time. The continuous-time case is a convention about events in time: $\delta_{X_F}(\varphi^u_x(t))\,dt$ stands for the unit point mass $\delta_{t_f}(dt)$ at the failure instant. A spatial Dirac composed with the trajectory would not give this: for a scalar crossing of $x_F$ at speed $\dot x(t_f) \ne 0$, $\int \delta(x(t) - x_F)\,dt = 1/|\dot x(t_f)|$, and a general closed set $X_F$ has no canonical Dirac distribution at all. Then $u$ is safe for $x$ if, and only if, $\rho(x,u) = 0$.

The only rule about point masses used below is $\int g(t)\,\delta_{t_f}(dt)=g(t_f)$: a unit mass in time samples the integrand at the event time. (The spatial comparison is a side remark: near a simple crossing $x(t)-x_F\approx\dot x(t_f)(t-t_f)$, and the substitution $s=\dot x(t_f)(t-t_f)$ turns $\int\delta(x(t)-x_F)\,dt$ into $\int\delta(s)\,ds/|\dot x(t_f)|=1/|\dot x(t_f)|$, a charge that would depend on the crossing speed instead of being one fixed penalty.)

Proof. With the sink convention the trajectory is in $X_F$ at exactly one instant, its time-to-failure $t_f \in \mathbb{T} \cup \{\infty\}$, so with this convention the integral evaluates to $\rho(x,u) = e^{-t_f/\tau}$ (and to $0$ if $t_f = \infty$). By definition $u$ is safe for $x$ iff the trajectory never enters $X_F$, i.e. iff $t_f = \infty$. $\square$

The discount inside $\rho$ is not needed for the lemma; it is there so that $\rho$ can be combined linearly with the return $G$, which has the same discount.
Key equation — The constrained problem (C) and the penalised problem (P)
The task is to maximise the expected return over safe controllers, for an initial distribution $\mu$ supported in $X_V$ (see Primer C): $$\text{(C)} \qquad \sup_{u \in \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{safe}}} \mathbb{E}_{x \sim \mu}\big[G(x,u)\big], \qquad\qquad V : x \in X_V \mapsto \sup_{u \in \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{safe}}} G(x,u),$$ where $V$ is the constrained value function, defined on the kernel only. Since constrained optimal control is hard, common practice relaxes the constraint and penalises failure by replacing $r$ with $r - p\,\delta_{X_F}$ for a constant designer-chosen penalty $p \in \mathbb{R}_+$: $$\text{(P)} \qquad V_p : x \in X \mapsto \sup_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \big[G(x,u) - p\,\rho(x,u)\big].$$ The supremum in (P) is assumed to be attained; its maximisers are the optimal controllers of $V_p$. Attainment is meant uniformly: there is a feedback controller that attains $V_p(x)$ at every $x$ at once (the paper's proof starts from "any controller that achieves $V_p$ for all $x$"; on finite deterministic problems dynamic programming supplies a stationary one). Problem 1: under what conditions on $p$ are the solutions of (P) both safe and optimal for (C)?

Assumption 1 — Uniformly bounded time-to-failure
The time-to-failure in $X_U$ is uniformly upper bounded by some $T_f \in \mathbb{T}$: for every $x \in X_U$ and every controller $u$, the trajectory $\varphi^u_x$ enters $X_F$ at a time $t_f(x,u) \le T_f$. $T_f$ is the time-scale of failure of the system; viability theory only says $t_f$ is finite, the assumption asks for a common bound.
Lemma — Influence of the penalty (Massiani et al., Lemma 2)
Under Assumption 1: (i) for every $x \in X$ the map $p \mapsto V_p(x)$ is nonincreasing; (ii) the value function is uniformly upper bounded on $X_U$, $$\begin{aligned} \sup_{X_U} V_p &\le R_{X_U}\, \tau \big(1 - e^{-T_f/\tau}\big) - p\, e^{-T_f/\tau} && (\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}_+), \\ \sup_{X_U} V_p &\le R_{X_U}\, \frac{1 - \gamma^{T_f + 1}}{1 - \gamma} - p\, \gamma^{T_f} && (\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{N}), \end{aligned}$$ with $R_{X_U} = \sup_{X_U \times U} r$.

Proof. (i): the supremum over $\mathcal{U}$ preserves the pointwise inequality $G - p_2 \rho \le G - p_1 \rho$ for $p_2 \ge p_1$, since $\rho \ge 0$. (ii): for $x \in X_U$, $V_p(x) \le \sup_u G(x,u) - p \inf_u \rho(x,u)$ because the supremum of a difference is at most the difference of supremum and infimum. Every trajectory from $x$ fails by time $T_f$ and collects nothing afterwards, so $G(x,u) \le R_{X_U} \int_0^{T_f} e^{-t/\tau} dt = R_{X_U}\tau(1 - e^{-T_f/\tau})$ (continuous) or $R_{X_U} \sum_{t=0}^{T_f} \gamma^t$ (discrete, reward collected at times $0, \dots, T_f$); and $\rho(x,u) = e^{-t_f/\tau} \ge e^{-T_f/\tau}$. The walkthrough below goes through every step. $\square$

Common mistake — $R_{X_U}$ is never negative
The bound on the reward part uses $R_{X_U} \ge 0$: it upper-bounds $\sum_{t \le t_f} \gamma^t r_t$ by $R_{X_U} \sum_{t \le T_f} \gamma^t$, which only holds if adding the terms between $t_f$ and $T_f$ cannot decrease the right-hand side. The paper does not state this sign condition; it holds in its examples because the failure states themselves carry zero reward ($r(-L) = 0$ on the shelf) and $X_F \subset X_U$. With a living cost $r = -c$ on the whole unviable region, failure states included, it is tempting to plug in $R_{X_U} = -c$; that gives a bound that is false (the agent can fail early and stop paying). Use $R_{X_U} = \max\{0, \sup_{X_U \times U} r\}$. No sign condition is needed for $R_{Q_U}$ and $R_{Q_V}$, which enter (Zb) through a single transition. In the explorer the cliff cells have zero reward, so its $R_{X_U}$ is automatically non-negative.

The point of Lemma 2 is (ii): the supremum of $V_p$ on the unviability kernel can be pushed arbitrarily low by increasing $p$, while $\inf_{X_V} V$ does not depend on $p$ at all. So (Z) can always be enforced.

Theorem — A finite penalty threshold (Massiani et al., Thm. 2)
Under Assumption 1 there exists a finite threshold $p^\star \in \mathbb{R}$ such that for all penalties $p \ge 0$ with $p \gt p^\star$ the penalised value function $V_p$ is safe and the zeroth-order condition (Z) holds, with $$p^\star = \Big(R_{X_U}\,\tau - \inf_{X_V} V\Big)\, e^{T_f/\tau} - R_{X_U}\,\tau \qquad (\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}_+),$$

Exercise 7.2 — Prove Lemma 2(ii) in discrete time

Under Assumption 1 with $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{N}$, prove that $\sup_{X_U} V_p \le R_{X_U}\frac{1 - \gamma^{T_f+1}}{1-\gamma} - p\,\gamma^{T_f}$, and state precisely where $R_{X_U} \ge 0$ is used. Then verify the bound on an upper slope cell of the explorer (row 2, zero slip), where $r = -c$ until the fall.

Show answer

Fix $x \in X_U$ and a controller $u$. Let $t_f \le T_f$ be the time at which the trajectory enters $X_F$; the state at time $t_f$ is a failure state (part of $X_U$), and from $t_f + 1$ on the system sits in the zero-reward sink. With the counting measure, $$G(x,u) = \sum_{t=0}^{t_f} \gamma^t r(x_t, u_t) \ \le\ R_{X_U}\sum_{t=0}^{t_f}\gamma^t \ \le\ R_{X_U}\sum_{t=0}^{T_f}\gamma^t = R_{X_U}\,\frac{1 - \gamma^{T_f+1}}{1-\gamma},$$ where the first inequality uses $r \le R_{X_U}$ on $X_U \times U$ (every visited state is unviable) and the second uses $R_{X_U} \ge 0$: extending the sum from $t_f$ to $T_f$ adds terms $\gamma^t R_{X_U} \ge 0$. If $R_{X_U}$ were negative the second inequality would reverse. Next, $\rho(x,u) = \sum_t \gamma^t \mathbf{1}_{X_F}(x_t) = \gamma^{t_f} \ge \gamma^{T_f}$ since $\gamma \lt 1$ and $t_f \le T_f$. Hence $G(x,u) - p\rho(x,u) \le R_{X_U}\frac{1-\gamma^{T_f+1}}{1-\gamma} - p\gamma^{T_f}$ for every $u$, and taking the supremum over $u$ and then over $x \in X_U$ gives the claim. $\square$

Check on the explorer's upper slope cell $(2,3)$ with zero slip. Moving down falls at once (the move and the slide add up to two rows), which is worth $-c - \gamma p$; any other move slides onto a lower slope cell, from which every action falls in one step, which is worth $-c + \gamma(-c - \gamma p) = -c - \gamma c - \gamma^2 p$. Hence $V_p(2,3) = \max\{-c - \gamma p,\ -c - \gamma c - \gamma^2 p\}$, and the slow fall wins iff $c \lt p(1 - \gamma)$. The bound with $T_f = 2$ and $R_{X_U} = \max\{0, -c\} = 0$ reads $V_p \le -p\gamma^2$, and both candidates satisfy it: $-c - \gamma p \le -\gamma^2 p$ because $-c \le 0 \le \gamma p (1 - \gamma)$, and $-c(1+\gamma) - \gamma^2 p \le -\gamma^2 p$. Had we used $R_{X_U} = -c$, the "bound" $-c(1 + \gamma + \gamma^2) - p\gamma^2$ would lie $\gamma^2 c$ below the slow-fall value, hence below $V_p(2,3)$ whenever $c \gt 0$: false.

import SafeLearning.CompleteModulesValues
import SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsGraphViability

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section
open Set MeasureTheory

/-!
TMP future27 draft, not compiled or selected.
The grid follows viability.html's ROWS=5/COLS=8/CLIFF=4,
ACTS=[Up,Down,Left,Right,Stay], source-cell slope slide, and zero-slip semantics.
All cliff coordinates are collapsed to the one failure event, followed by
an explicit zero-reward sink. No candidate return is a hypothesis.
-/
namespace SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedExplorerSlope27

inductive Action where
  | up | down | left | right | stay
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

inductive State where
  | live (row : Fin 4) (col : Fin 8)
  | failure | sink
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- The exact six source-cell slope locations. -/
def slope (row col : ℕ) : Bool :=
  (row == 3 && decide (2 ≤ col ∧ col ≤ 5)) || (row == 2 && (col == 3 || col == 4))

/-- Nat subtraction implements JS's lower clamp for the Up/Left actions. -/
def movedRow (row : ℕ) : Action → ℕ
  | .up => row - 1
  | .down => min 4 (row + 1)
  | _ => row

def movedCol (col : ℕ) : Action → ℕ
  | .left => col - 1
  | .right => min 7 (col + 1)
  | _ => col

def cell (row col : ℕ) : State :=
  .live ⟨min 3 row, by omega⟩ ⟨min 7 col, by omega⟩

def step : State → Action → State
  | .failure, _ => .sink
  | .sink, _ => .sink
  | .live row col, a =>
      let row' := if slope row.val col.val then min 4 (movedRow row.val a + 1)
                    else movedRow row.val a
      let col' := movedCol col.val a
      if row' = 4 then .failure else cell row' col'

def available : State → Action → Prop
  | .live row col, a => slope row.val col.val = false ∨ a ≠ .up
  | _, _ => True

def upper : State := cell 2 3

def lowerLeft : State := cell 3 2

def lowerCenter : State := cell 3 3

def lowerRight : State := cell 3 4

/-- The literal reward function, including zero reward at failure and sink. -/
def reward (cost goalReward : ℝ) : State → ℝ
  | .live row col => if row.val = 3 ∧ col.val = 7 then goalReward else -cost
  | _ => 0

def failureCharge : State → ℝ
  | .failure => 1
  | _ => 0

/-- The post-failure sink is bookkeeping, excluded from the physical world. -/
def world : Set State := {s | s ≠ .sink}

def safeStates : Set State := {s | match s with
  | .live _ _ => True
  | _ => False}

def kernelStates : Set State := {s | match s with
  | .live row col => slope row.val col.val = false
  | _ => False}

def unviableStates : Set State := world \ kernelStates

theorem actual_nonslope_stay_is_safe_self_loop (row : Fin 4) (col : Fin 8)
    (hs : slope row.val col.val = false) :
    step (.live row col) .stay = .live row col := by
  have hr : row.val ≤ 3 := by omega
  have hc : col.val ≤ 7 := by omega
  have hr4 : row.val ≠ 4 := by omega
  simp [step, hs, movedRow, movedCol, cell, hr4,
    Nat.min_eq_right hr, Nat.min_eq_right hc]

theorem actual_grid_kernel_is_greatest_control_invariant :
    IsGreatest {Y : Set State | Y ⊆ safeStates ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre step available Y} kernelStates := by
  refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro s hs
    cases s <;> simp_all [safeStates, kernelStates]
  · intro s hs
    cases s with
    | live row col =>
      exact ⟨.stay, by simp [available], by
        rw [actual_nonslope_stay_is_safe_self_loop row col hs]
        exact hs⟩
    | failure => simp [kernelStates] at hs
    | sink => simp [kernelStates] at hs
  · rintro Y ⟨hYs, hY⟩ s hs
    cases s with
    | live row col =>
      change slope row.val col.val = false
      by_contra hnonslope
      obtain ⟨a, ha, hnext⟩ := hY hs
      obtain ⟨b, hb, hnext2⟩ := hY hnext
      have hsafe1 := hYs hnext
      have hsafe2 := hYs hnext2
      fin_cases row <;> fin_cases col <;> cases a <;> cases b <;>
        simp_all [safeStates, kernelStates, available, step, cell,
          slope, movedRow, movedCol]
    | failure => simpa [safeStates, kernelStates] using hYs hs
    | sink => simpa [safeStates, kernelStates] using hYs hs

theorem actual_grid_kernel_is_exact_all_time_viability (initial : State) :
    initial ∈ kernelStates ↔ ∃ states : ℕ → State, ∃ actions : ℕ → Action,
      states 0 = initial ∧ ∀ n, states n ∈ safeStates ∧
        available (states n) (actions n) ∧ states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n) := by
  exact CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.actual_greatest_control_invariant_set_is_the_true_all_time_viability_kernel
    step available safeStates kernelStates actual_grid_kernel_is_greatest_control_invariant initial

theorem actual_unviable_reward_is_nonpositive (cost goalReward : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ cost)
    (s : State) (hs : s ∈ unviableStates) : reward cost goalReward s ≤ 0 := by
  cases s with
  | live row col =>
    by_cases hg : row.val = 3 ∧ col.val = 7
    · have hk : State.live row col ∈ kernelStates := by
        simp [kernelStates, slope, hg.1, hg.2]
      exact False.elim (hs.2 hk)
    · simpa [reward, hg] using neg_nonpos.mpr hc
  | failure => simp [reward]
  | sink => simp [reward]

theorem actual_unviable_reward_supremum_is_zero (cost goalReward : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ cost) :
    sSup (reward cost goalReward '' unviableStates) = 0 := by
  apply IsGreatest.csSup_eq
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · exact ⟨.failure, by simp [unviableStates, world, kernelStates], by simp [reward]⟩
  · rintro _ ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩
    exact actual_unviable_reward_is_nonpositive _ _ hc s hs

theorem actual_unviable_state_action_reward_supremum_is_zero
    (cost goalReward : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ cost) :
    sSup (Set.range (fun q : unviableStates × Action => reward cost goalReward q.1.val)) = 0 := by
  have he : Set.range (fun q : unviableStates × Action => reward cost goalReward q.1.val) =
      reward cost goalReward '' unviableStates := by
    ext v
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨⟨state, hs⟩, action⟩, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨state, hs, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨state, hs, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨(⟨state, hs⟩, .down), rfl⟩
  rw [he]
  exact actual_unviable_reward_supremum_is_zero cost goalReward hc

def discountedReward (discount cost goalReward : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State) : ℝ :=
  ∑' n, discount ^ n * reward cost goalReward (states n)

def discountedRisk (discount : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State) : ℝ :=
  ∑' n, discount ^ n * failureCharge (states n)

def penalizedReturn (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State) : ℝ :=
  discountedReward discount cost goalReward states - penalty * discountedRisk discount states

/-- Every realized admissible control path, not an asserted list of candidate rewards. -/
def Realizes (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action) : Prop :=
  states 0 = upper ∧
  (∀ n, available (states n) (actions n)) ∧
  ∀ n, states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n)

theorem actual_upper_available_iff (a : Action) : available upper a ↔ a ≠ .up := by
  simp [available, upper, cell, slope]

theorem actual_upper_successor_table :
    step upper .down = .failure ∧ step upper .left = lowerLeft ∧
    step upper .right = lowerRight ∧ step upper .stay = lowerCenter := by
  norm_num [step, upper, lowerLeft, lowerRight, lowerCenter, cell, slope,
    movedRow, movedCol]

theorem actual_every_lower_action_falls (s : State) (a : Action)
    (hs : s = lowerLeft ∨ s = lowerCenter ∨ s = lowerRight)
    (ha : available s a) : step s a = .failure := by
  rcases hs with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    cases a <;>
    simp_all [available, step, lowerLeft, lowerCenter, lowerRight,
      cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol]

theorem actual_sink_tail (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action) (start : ℕ)
    (hs : states start = .sink)
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n)) :
    ∀ n, start ≤ n → states n = .sink := by
  have htail : ∀ d, states (start + d) = .sink := by
    intro d
    induction d with
    | zero => simpa using hs
    | succ d ih =>
        rw [show start + (d + 1) = (start + d) + 1 by omega, hstep, ih]
        rfl
  intro n hn
  have he : n = start + (n - start) := by omega
  rw [he]
  exact htail _

theorem actual_every_unviable_grid_path_fails_by_two
    (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action)
    (hzero : states 0 ∈ unviableStates)
    (hlegal : ∀ n, available (states n) (actions n))
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n)) :
    ∃ failure ≤ 2, states failure = .failure ∧
      ∀ n, failure < n → states n = .sink := by
  by_cases h0 : states 0 = .failure
  · refine ⟨0, by omega, h0, ?_⟩
    have hsink : states 1 = .sink := by simpa [h0, step] using hstep 0
    intro n hn
    exact actual_sink_tail states actions 1 hsink hstep n (by omega)
  · have hearly : states 1 = .failure ∨ states 2 = .failure := by
      have h1 := hstep 0
      have h2 := hstep 1
      have ha := hlegal 0
      have hb := hlegal 1
      cases hs : states 0 with
      | failure => exact False.elim (h0 hs)
      | sink => simp [hs, unviableStates, world] at hzero
      | live row col =>
        cases ha0 : actions 0 <;> cases ha1 : actions 1 <;>
          fin_cases row <;> fin_cases col <;>
          simp_all [unviableStates, world, kernelStates, available,
            step, cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol]
    rcases hearly with h1 | h2
    · refine ⟨1, by omega, h1, ?_⟩
      have hsink : states 2 = .sink := by simpa [h1, step] using hstep 1
      intro n hn
      exact actual_sink_tail states actions 2 hsink hstep n (by omega)
    · refine ⟨2, by omega, h2, ?_⟩
      have hsink : states 3 = .sink := by simpa [h2, step] using hstep 2
      intro n hn
      exact actual_sink_tail states actions 3 hsink hstep n (by omega)

/-- The literal transition to the sink makes the failure event one-time. -/
theorem actual_grid_failure_is_visited_at_exactly_one_time
    (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action) (failure : ℕ)
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n))
    (hhit : states failure = .failure) :
    ∀ n, states n = .failure ↔ n = failure := by
  have hsink : states (failure + 1) = .sink := by
    rw [hstep, hhit]
    rfl
  have htail := actual_sink_tail states actions (failure + 1) hsink hstep
  intro n
  constructor
  · intro hnfail
    by_contra hn
    by_cases hlt : n < failure
    · have hnsink : states (n + 1) = .sink := by rw [hstep, hnfail]; rfl
      have htf := actual_sink_tail states actions (n + 1) hnsink hstep failure (by omega)
      rw [hhit] at htf
      contradiction
    · have hnsink := htail n (by omega)
      rw [hnfail] at hnsink
      contradiction
  · rintro rfl
    exact hhit

theorem actual_every_upper_path_has_the_two_failure_patterns
    (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action) (h : Realizes states actions) :
    (actions 0 = .down ∧ states 1 = .failure ∧ ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → states n = .sink) ∨
    (actions 0 ≠ .down ∧
      (states 1 = lowerLeft ∨ states 1 = lowerCenter ∨ states 1 = lowerRight) ∧
      states 2 = .failure ∧ ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → states n = .sink) := by
  rcases h with ⟨hzero, hlegal, hstep⟩
  have hfirst : states 1 = step upper (actions 0) := by simpa [hzero] using hstep 0
  have haction : actions 0 ≠ .up :=
    (actual_upper_available_iff _).mp (by simpa [hzero] using hlegal 0)
  by_cases hd : actions 0 = .down
  · left
    have hfailure : states 1 = .failure := by
      rw [hfirst, hd, actual_upper_successor_table.1]
    have hsink : states 2 = .sink := by
      simpa [hfailure, step] using hstep 1
    exact ⟨hd, hfailure, actual_sink_tail states actions 2 hsink hstep⟩
  · right
    have hlower : states 1 = lowerLeft ∨ states 1 = lowerCenter ∨ states 1 = lowerRight := by
      rw [hfirst]
      cases he : actions 0 <;>
        simp_all [step, upper, lowerLeft, lowerCenter, lowerRight,
          cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol]
    have hfailure : states 2 = .failure := by
      rw [hstep 1]
      exact actual_every_lower_action_falls _ _ hlower (hlegal 1)
    have hsink : states 3 = .sink := by
      simpa [hfailure, step] using hstep 2
    exact ⟨hd, hlower, hfailure, actual_sink_tail states actions 3 hsink hstep⟩

/-- Both infinite sums are genuine finite-support sums of the actual states. -/
theorem actual_three_term_counting_sums
    (discount cost goalReward : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State)
    (htail : ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → states n = .sink) :
    discountedReward discount cost goalReward states =
      reward cost goalReward (states 0) + discount * reward cost goalReward (states 1) +
        discount ^ 2 * reward cost goalReward (states 2) ∧
    discountedRisk discount states =
      failureCharge (states 0) + discount * failureCharge (states 1) +
        discount ^ 2 * failureCharge (states 2) := by
  constructor
  · rw [discountedReward, tsum_eq_sum (s := Finset.range 3)]
    · norm_num [Finset.sum_range_succ]
    · intro n hn
      have hn3 : 3 ≤ n := by simpa only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] using hn
      simp [htail n hn3, reward]
  · rw [discountedRisk, tsum_eq_sum (s := Finset.range 3)]
    · norm_num [Finset.sum_range_succ]
    · intro n hn
      have hn3 : 3 ≤ n := by simpa only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] using hn
      simp [htail n hn3, failureCharge]

theorem actual_every_upper_path_return_is_fast_or_slow
    (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action)
    (h : Realizes states actions) :
    penalizedReturn discount cost goalReward penalty states = -cost - discount * penalty ∨
    penalizedReturn discount cost goalReward penalty states =
      -cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty := by
  have hzero := h.1
  rcases actual_every_upper_path_has_the_two_failure_patterns states actions h with
    ⟨_, hfailure, htail⟩ | ⟨_, hlower, hfailure, htail⟩
  · left
    have hsink : states 2 = .sink := htail 2 (by omega)
    have hsums := actual_three_term_counting_sums discount cost goalReward states
      (fun n hn => htail n (by omega))
    rw [penalizedReturn, hsums.1, hsums.2, hzero, hfailure, hsink]
    norm_num [reward, failureCharge, upper, cell]
  · right
    have hsums := actual_three_term_counting_sums discount cost goalReward states htail
    rw [penalizedReturn, hsums.1, hsums.2, hzero, hfailure]
    rcases hlower with hleft | hcenter | hright <;>
      simp_all [reward, failureCharge,
        upper, lowerLeft, lowerCenter, lowerRight, cell] <;> ring

structure Feedback where
  choose : State → Action
  legal : ∀ s, available s (choose s)

def feedbackStates (controller : Feedback) : ℕ → State
  | 0 => upper
  | n + 1 => step (feedbackStates controller n) (controller.choose (feedbackStates controller n))

def feedbackActions (controller : Feedback) (n : ℕ) : Action :=
  controller.choose (feedbackStates controller n)

def downFeedback : Feedback :=
  ⟨fun _ => .down, by intro s; cases s <;> simp [available]⟩

def stayFeedback : Feedback :=
  ⟨fun _ => .stay, by intro s; cases s <;> simp [available]⟩

def controllerReturn (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) (controller : Feedback) : ℝ :=
  penalizedReturn discount cost goalReward penalty (feedbackStates controller)

def actualUpperValue (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sSup (Set.range (controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty))

theorem actual_every_feedback_realizes_its_path (controller : Feedback) :
    Realizes (feedbackStates controller) (feedbackActions controller) := by
  exact ⟨rfl, fun n => controller.legal _, fun _ => rfl⟩

theorem actual_down_feedback_attains_fast (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) :
    controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty downFeedback = -cost - discount * penalty := by
  have hsink : ∀ n, 2 ≤ n → feedbackStates downFeedback n = .sink :=
    actual_sink_tail _ _ 2 (by
      norm_num [feedbackStates, downFeedback, step, upper, cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol])
      (actual_every_feedback_realizes_its_path downFeedback).2.2
  have hsums := actual_three_term_counting_sums discount cost goalReward (feedbackStates downFeedback)
    (fun n hn => hsink n (by omega))
  rw [controllerReturn, penalizedReturn, hsums.1, hsums.2]
  norm_num [feedbackStates, downFeedback, reward, failureCharge, step,
    upper, cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol]

theorem actual_stay_feedback_attains_slow (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) :
    controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty stayFeedback =
      -cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty := by
  have hsink : ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → feedbackStates stayFeedback n = .sink :=
    actual_sink_tail _ _ 3 (by
      norm_num [feedbackStates, stayFeedback, step, upper, cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol])
      (actual_every_feedback_realizes_its_path stayFeedback).2.2
  have hsums := actual_three_term_counting_sums discount cost goalReward (feedbackStates stayFeedback) hsink
  rw [controllerReturn, penalizedReturn, hsums.1, hsums.2]
  norm_num [feedbackStates, stayFeedback, reward, failureCharge, step,
    upper, cell, slope, movedRow, movedCol]
  ring

theorem actual_controller_return_set_is_exactly_the_two_source_values
    (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) :
    Set.range (controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty) =
      {-cost - discount * penalty, -cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty} := by
  ext v
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨controller, rfl⟩
    have hv := actual_every_upper_path_return_is_fast_or_slow discount cost goalReward penalty
      (feedbackStates controller) (feedbackActions controller)
      (actual_every_feedback_realizes_its_path controller)
    simpa [controllerReturn, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] using hv
  · intro hv
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hv
    rcases hv with rfl | rfl
    · exact ⟨downFeedback, actual_down_feedback_attains_fast _ _ _ _⟩
    · exact ⟨stayFeedback, actual_stay_feedback_attains_slow _ _ _ _⟩

theorem actual_controller_supremum_is_attained_source_max
    (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) :
    actualUpperValue discount cost goalReward penalty =
      max (-cost - discount * penalty) (-cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty) := by
  unfold actualUpperValue
  rw [actual_controller_return_set_is_exactly_the_two_source_values]
  exact csSup_pair _ _

theorem actual_stopped_reward_and_negative_bound_difference (discount cost penalty : ℝ) :
    (-cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty) -
      (-cost * (1 + discount + discount ^ 2) - penalty * discount ^ 2) = discount ^ 2 * cost ∧
    -cost + discount * (-cost - discount * penalty) =
      -cost - discount * cost - discount ^ 2 * penalty := by
  constructor <;> ring

theorem actual_slope_value_has_the_source_bound (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount ≤ 1) (hc : 0 ≤ cost) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty) :
    actualUpperValue discount cost goalReward penalty ≤ -penalty * discount ^ 2 := by
  rw [actual_controller_supremum_is_attained_source_max]
  exact CompleteModulesValues.two_step_slope_bound _ _ _ hd hd1 hc hp

theorem actual_slow_fall_strictly_wins_exactly_when_printed
    (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) (hd : 0 < discount) :
    controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty downFeedback <
      controllerReturn discount cost goalReward penalty stayFeedback ↔ cost < penalty * (1 - discount) := by
  rw [actual_down_feedback_attains_fast, actual_stay_feedback_attains_slow]
  exact CompleteModulesValues.slow_slope_strictly_better _ _ _ hd

theorem actual_nonnegative_reward_constant (cost : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ cost) :
    max 0 (-cost) = 0 := by simp [max_eq_left (by linarith : -cost ≤ 0)]

theorem actual_negative_reward_bound_is_below_the_value
    (discount cost goalReward penalty : ℝ) (hd : 0 < discount) (hc : 0 < cost) :
    -cost * (1 + discount + discount ^ 2) - penalty * discount ^ 2 <
      actualUpperValue discount cost goalReward penalty := by
  rw [actual_controller_supremum_is_attained_source_max]
  exact lt_of_lt_of_le (CompleteModulesValues.negative_reward_slope_bound_false _ _ _ hd hc)
    (le_max_right _ _)

/-- A stopped sequence has the counting-measure reward exactly as printed. -/
theorem stopped_discounted_reward_is_finite_prefix (discount : ℝ) (rewards : ℕ → ℝ)
    (failure : ℕ) (hz : ∀ n, failure < n → rewards n = 0) :
    (∑' n, discount ^ n * rewards n) =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (failure + 1), discount ^ n * rewards n := by
  apply tsum_eq_sum
  intro n hn
  have hnf : failure < n := by
    have hn' : ¬n < failure + 1 := by simpa only [Finset.mem_range] using hn
    omega
  simp [hz n hnf]

/-- Finite support derives integrability, rather than making it an assumption. -/
theorem actual_finite_support_counting_integral_is_its_sum
    (terms : ℕ → ℝ) (length : ℕ) (hz : ∀ n, length ≤ n → terms n = 0) :
    Integrable terms Measure.count ∧
      (∫ n : ℕ, terms n ∂Measure.count) = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range length, terms n := by
  have hvanish (n : ℕ) (hn : n ∉ Finset.range length) : terms n = 0 := by
    apply hz n
    simpa only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] using hn
  have hnorm : Summable (fun n => ‖terms n‖) :=
    summable_of_ne_finset_zero (s := Finset.range length) (by
      intro n hn
      simp [hvanish n hn])
  have hi : Integrable terms Measure.count := integrable_count_iff.mpr hnorm
  refine ⟨hi, ?_⟩
  rw [integral_countable hi]
  simp only [measureReal_def, Measure.count_apply_singleton,
    ENNReal.toReal_one, one_smul]
  exact tsum_eq_sum hvanish

theorem actual_stopped_counting_integral_is_the_printed_finite_reward_sum
    (discount : ℝ) (rewards : ℕ → ℝ) (failure : ℕ)
    (hz : ∀ n, failure < n → rewards n = 0) :
    Integrable (fun n => discount ^ n * rewards n) Measure.count ∧
      (∫ n : ℕ, discount ^ n * rewards n ∂Measure.count) =
        ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (failure + 1), discount ^ n * rewards n := by
  apply actual_finite_support_counting_integral_is_its_sum
  intro n hn
  simp [hz n (by omega)]

theorem single_failure_discounted_risk_is_arrival_weight (discount : ℝ) (failure : ℕ) :
    (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) = discount ^ failure := by
  rw [tsum_eq_single failure]
  · simp
  · intro n hn
    simp [hn]

theorem actual_single_failure_counting_integral_is_arrival_weight
    (discount : ℝ) (failure : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun n : ℕ => discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) Measure.count ∧
      (∫ n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ) ∂Measure.count) =
        discount ^ failure := by
  have hvanish : ∀ n : ℕ, failure + 1 ≤ n →
      discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ) = 0 := by
    intro n hn
    simp [show n ≠ failure by omega]
  have hi := actual_finite_support_counting_integral_is_its_sum
    (fun n : ℕ => discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) (failure + 1) hvanish
  refine ⟨hi.1, ?_⟩
  rw [integral_countable hi.1]
  simp only [measureReal_def, Measure.count_apply_singleton,
    ENNReal.toReal_one, one_smul]
  exact single_failure_discounted_risk_is_arrival_weight _ _

/-- No one-time-charge or vanishing-tail assumption is needed for this actual grid path. -/
theorem actual_grid_arrival_derives_the_counting_reward_and_risk
    (discount cost goalReward : ℝ) (states : ℕ → State) (actions : ℕ → Action)
    (failure : ℕ) (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = step (states n) (actions n))
    (hhit : states failure = .failure) :
    discountedReward discount cost goalReward states =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (failure + 1), discount ^ n * reward cost goalReward (states n) ∧
    discountedRisk discount states = discount ^ failure := by
  have hsink : states (failure + 1) = .sink := by rw [hstep, hhit]; rfl
  have htail := actual_sink_tail states actions (failure + 1) hsink hstep
  have honce := actual_grid_failure_is_visited_at_exactly_one_time states actions failure hstep hhit
  constructor
  · apply stopped_discounted_reward_is_finite_prefix
    intro n hn
    simp [htail n (by omega), reward]
  · unfold discountedRisk
    have hcharge (n : ℕ) : failureCharge (states n) = (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ) := by
      by_cases hn : n = failure
      · subst n
        simp [hhit, failureCharge]
      · have hnf : states n ≠ .failure := fun h => hn ((honce n).mp h)
        cases he : states n <;> simp_all [failureCharge]
    simp_rw [hcharge]
    exact single_failure_discounted_risk_is_arrival_weight discount failure

theorem nonnegative_reward_bound_allows_horizon_extension
    (discount bound : ℝ) (failure horizon : ℕ) (hd : 0 ≤ discount)
    (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (ht : failure ≤ horizon) :
    bound * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (failure + 1), discount ^ n) ≤
      bound * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (horizon + 1), discount ^ n) := by
  apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ hb
  exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg
    (Finset.range_mono (by omega)) (by intros; positivity)

theorem negative_reward_bound_reverses_horizon_extension
    (discount bound : ℝ) (failure horizon : ℕ) (hd : 0 ≤ discount)
    (hb : bound ≤ 0) (ht : failure ≤ horizon) :
    bound * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (horizon + 1), discount ^ n) ≤
      bound * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (failure + 1), discount ^ n) := by
  apply mul_le_mul_of_nonpos_left _ hb
  exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg
    (Finset.range_mono (by omega)) (by intros; positivity)

theorem counting_sum_doomed_return_bound (discount bound penalty : ℝ)
    (rewards : ℕ → ℝ) (failure horizon : ℕ) (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1)
    (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty) (ht : failure ≤ horizon)
    (hr : ∀ n < failure + 1, rewards n ≤ bound)
    (hz : ∀ n, failure < n → rewards n = 0) :
    (∑' n, discount ^ n * rewards n) -
      penalty * (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if n = failure then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) ≤
      bound * (1 - discount ^ (horizon + 1)) / (1 - discount) - penalty * discount ^ horizon := by
  rw [stopped_discounted_reward_is_finite_prefix discount rewards failure hz,
    single_failure_discounted_risk_is_arrival_weight]
  exact CompleteModulesValues.finite_discounted_doomed_bound _ _ _ _ _ _ hd hd1 hb hp ht hr

/-- Adding a safe predecessor of the greatest invariant set cannot enlarge it. -/
theorem actual_unviability_is_forward_invariant_before_failure
    {S A : Type*} (dynamics : S → A → S) (allowed : S → A → Prop)
    (safe kernel : Set S)
    (hk : IsGreatest {Y : Set S | Y ⊆ safe ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed Y} kernel)
    (x : S) (a : A) (hx : x ∉ kernel) (hsafe : x ∈ safe) (ha : allowed x a) :
    dynamics x a ∉ kernel := by
  intro hnext
  have hgrown : insert x kernel ⊆ safe ∧ insert x kernel ⊆
      CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed (insert x kernel) := by
    constructor
    · intro y hy
      rcases hy with rfl | hy
      · exact hsafe
      · exact hk.1.1 hy
    · intro y hy
      rcases hy with rfl | hy
      · exact ⟨a, ha, Or.inr hnext⟩
      · obtain ⟨b, hb, hsuccessor⟩ := hk.1.2 hy
        exact ⟨b, hb, Or.inr hsuccessor⟩
  exact hx (hk.2 hgrown (by simp))

theorem actual_every_visited_prefailure_state_is_unviable
    {S A : Type*} (dynamics : S → A → S) (allowed : S → A → Prop)
    (safe kernel : Set S)
    (hk : IsGreatest {Y : Set S | Y ⊆ safe ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed Y} kernel)
    (states : ℕ → S) (actions : ℕ → A) (failure : ℕ)
    (hzero : states 0 ∉ kernel) (hsafe : ∀ n < failure, states n ∈ safe)
    (hallowed : ∀ n, allowed (states n) (actions n))
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = dynamics (states n) (actions n)) :
    ∀ n ≤ failure, states n ∉ kernel := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero => intro _; exact hzero
  | succ n ih =>
    intro hn
    rw [hstep n]
    exact actual_unviability_is_forward_invariant_before_failure dynamics allowed safe kernel hk
      _ _ (ih (by omega)) (hsafe n (by omega)) (hallowed n)

/-- The source's bound on X_U×U now supplies the actual visited reward bound. -/
theorem actual_unviable_trajectory_counting_sum_bound
    {S A : Type*} (dynamics : S → A → S) (allowed : S → A → Prop)
    (safe kernel failureStates : Set S)
    (hk : IsGreatest {Y : Set S | Y ⊆ safe ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed Y} kernel)
    (states : ℕ → S) (actions : ℕ → A) (r : S → A → ℝ)
    (discount bound penalty : ℝ) (failure horizon : ℕ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1) (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty)
    (ht : failure ≤ horizon) (hzero : states 0 ∉ kernel)
    (hsafe : ∀ n < failure, states n ∈ safe)
    (hallowed : ∀ n, allowed (states n) (actions n))
    (hstep : ∀ n, states (n + 1) = dynamics (states n) (actions n))
    (hr : ∀ x ∉ kernel, ∀ a, allowed x a → r x a ≤ bound)
    (hz : ∀ n, failure < n → r (states n) (actions n) = 0)
    (hfailure : ∀ n, states n ∈ failureStates ↔ n = failure) :
    (∑' n, discount ^ n * r (states n) (actions n)) -
      penalty * (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if states n ∈ failureStates then 1 else 0 : ℝ)) ≤
      bound * (1 - discount ^ (horizon + 1)) / (1 - discount) - penalty * discount ^ horizon := by
  have hvisited := actual_every_visited_prefailure_state_is_unviable dynamics allowed safe kernel hk
    states actions failure hzero hsafe hallowed hstep
  simp_rw [hfailure]
  apply counting_sum_doomed_return_bound _ _ _ _ _ _ hd hd1 hb hp ht
  · intro n hn
    exact hr (states n) (hvisited n (by omega)) (actions n) (hallowed n)
  · exact hz

theorem both_controller_and_state_suprema_preserve_counting_sum_bound
    {X Controller : Type*} [Nonempty X] [Nonempty Controller]
    (discount bound penalty : ℝ) (rewards : X → Controller → ℕ → ℝ)
    (failure : X → Controller → ℕ) (horizon : ℕ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1) (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty)
    (ht : ∀ x u, failure x u ≤ horizon)
    (hr : ∀ x u n, n < failure x u + 1 → rewards x u n ≤ bound)
    (hz : ∀ x u n, failure x u < n → rewards x u n = 0) :
    sSup (Set.range (fun x => sSup (Set.range (fun u =>
      (∑' n, discount ^ n * rewards x u n) - penalty *
        (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if n = failure x u then 1 else 0 : ℝ)))))) ≤
      bound * (1 - discount ^ (horizon + 1)) / (1 - discount) - penalty * discount ^ horizon := by
  apply CompleteModulesValues.supremum_doomed_bound
  · exact Set.range_nonempty _
  · intro x
    apply CompleteModulesValues.supremum_doomed_bound
    · exact Set.range_nonempty _
    · intro u
      exact counting_sum_doomed_return_bound _ _ _ _ _ _ hd hd1 hb hp (ht x u)
        (hr x u) (hz x u)

/-- This is the source supremum convention even when the unviable set is empty.
For a nonempty set it coincides with the real-valued outer supremum above. -/
theorem source_extended_outer_supremum_preserves_the_uniform_doomed_bound
    {X Controller : Type*} [Nonempty Controller]
    (discount bound penalty : ℝ) (rewards : X → Controller → ℕ → ℝ)
    (failure : X → Controller → ℕ) (horizon : ℕ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1) (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty)
    (ht : ∀ x u, failure x u ≤ horizon)
    (hr : ∀ x u n, n < failure x u + 1 → rewards x u n ≤ bound)
    (hz : ∀ x u n, failure x u < n → rewards x u n = 0) :
    sSup (Set.range (fun x => ((sSup (Set.range (fun u =>
      (∑' n, discount ^ n * rewards x u n) - penalty *
        (∑' n : ℕ, discount ^ n * (if n = failure x u then 1 else 0 : ℝ))))) : ℝ) : EReal))) ≤
      ((bound * (1 - discount ^ (horizon + 1)) / (1 - discount) -
        penalty * discount ^ horizon : ℝ) : EReal) := by
  apply sSup_le
  rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
  apply EReal.coe_le_coe
  apply CompleteModulesValues.supremum_doomed_bound
  · exact Set.range_nonempty _
  · intro u
    exact counting_sum_doomed_return_bound _ _ _ _ _ _ hd hd1 hb hp (ht x u)
      (hr x u) (hz x u)

/-- The source reward supremum is over physical unviable states, not the
post-failure bookkeeping sink. Boundedness comes from the source reward scope. -/
theorem actual_reward_supremum_bounds_each_physical_unviable_state_action
    {S A : Type*} (physical kernel : Set S) (r : S → A → ℝ)
    (hbounded : BddAbove (Set.range (fun q : (physical \ kernel) × A => r q.1.val q.2)))
    (x : S) (hx : x ∈ physical) (hxk : x ∉ kernel) (a : A) :
    r x a ≤ sSup (Set.range (fun q : (physical \ kernel) × A => r q.1.val q.2)) := by
  exact le_csSup hbounded ⟨(⟨x, ⟨hx, hxk⟩⟩, a), rfl⟩

/-- Every visited reward bound is derived from the actual physical-state
supremum and the greatest-kernel property; no bound outside the world is
required. The explicit arrival and sink semantics match the source. -/
theorem source_physical_unviable_trajectory_counting_sum_bound
    {S A : Type*} (dynamics : S → A → S) (allowed : S → A → Prop)
    (physical safe kernel failureStates : Set S)
    (hk : IsGreatest {Y : Set S | Y ⊆ safe ∧
      Y ⊆ CompleteFoundationsGraphViability.controlledPre dynamics allowed Y} kernel)

Exercise 7.2 — Prove Lemma 2(ii) in discrete time
      
        Under Assumption 1 with $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{N}$, prove that $\sup_{X_U} V_p \le R_{X_U}\frac{1 - \gamma^{T_f+1}}{1-\gamma} - p\,\gamma^{T_f}$, and state precisely where $R_{X_U} \ge 0$ is used. Then verify the bound on an upper slope cell of the explorer (row 2, zero slip), where $r = -c$ until the fall.
        
          Show answer
          
            Fix $x \in X_U$ and a controller $u$. Let $t_f \le T_f$ be the time at which the trajectory enters $X_F$; the state at time $t_f$ is a failure state (part of $X_U$), and from $t_f + 1$ on the system sits in the zero-reward sink. With the counting measure,
              $$G(x,u) = \sum_{t=0}^{t_f} \gamma^t r(x_t, u_t) \ \le\ R_{X_U}\sum_{t=0}^{t_f}\gamma^t \ \le\ R_{X_U}\sum_{t=0}^{T_f}\gamma^t = R_{X_U}\,\frac{1 - \gamma^{T_f+1}}{1-\gamma},$$
              where the first inequality uses $r \le R_{X_U}$ on $X_U \times U$ (every visited state is unviable) and the second uses $R_{X_U} \ge 0$: extending the sum from $t_f$ to $T_f$ adds terms $\gamma^t R_{X_U} \ge 0$. If $R_{X_U}$ were negative the second inequality would reverse. Next, $\rho(x,u) = \sum_t \gamma^t \mathbf{1}_{X_F}(x_t) = \gamma^{t_f} \ge \gamma^{T_f}$ since $\gamma \lt 1$ and $t_f \le T_f$. Hence $G(x,u) - p\rho(x,u) \le R_{X_U}\frac{1-\gamma^{T_f+1}}{1-\gamma} - p\gamma^{T_f}$ for every $u$, and taking the supremum over $u$ and then over $x \in X_U$ gives the claim. $\square$
            Check on the explorer's upper slope cell $(2,3)$ with zero slip. Moving down falls at once (the move and the slide add up to two rows), which is worth $-c - \gamma p$; any other move slides onto a lower slope cell, from which every action falls in one step, which is worth $-c + \gamma(-c - \gamma p) = -c - \gamma c - \gamma^2 p$. import SafeLearning.Modules
import SafeLearning.BookApplications

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section
open Set
namespace SafeLearning.CompleteModulesValues

theorem finite_discounted_doomed_bound (reward : ℕ → ℝ) (discount bound penalty : ℝ)
    (failure horizon : ℕ) (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount < 1)
    (hb : 0 ≤ bound) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty) (ht : failure ≤ horizon)
    (hr : ∀ t < failure+1, reward t ≤ bound) :
    (∑ t ∈ Finset.range (failure+1), discount^t*reward t)-penalty*discount^failure ≤
      bound*(1-discount^(horizon+1))/(1-discount)-penalty*discount^horizon := by
  have hreward : (∑ t ∈ Finset.range (failure+1), discount^t*reward t) ≤
      ∑ t ∈ Finset.range (horizon+1), discount^t*bound := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ t ∈ Finset.range (failure+1), discount^t*bound := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro t hm
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hr t (Finset.mem_range.mp hm)) (pow_nonneg hd t)
      _ ≤ _ := Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg
        (Finset.range_mono (Nat.add_le_add_right ht 1)) (by intros; positivity)
  have hpenalty : penalty*discount^horizon ≤ penalty*discount^failure :=
    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (pow_le_pow_of_le_one hd (le_of_lt hd1) ht) hp
  have hgeom : (∑ t ∈ Finset.range (horizon+1), discount^t*bound)=
      bound*(1-discount^(horizon+1))/(1-discount) := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_mul,geom_sum_eq (ne_of_lt hd1)]
    rw [show discount-1=-(1-discount) by ring,div_neg]
    ring
  rw [hgeom] at hreward
  linarith

theorem supremum_doomed_bound {X : Type*} (returns : X → ℝ) (upper : ℝ)
    (hne : (Set.range returns).Nonempty) (h : ∀ x, returns x ≤ upper) :
    sSup (Set.range returns) ≤ upper := by
  apply csSup_le hne
  rintro _ ⟨x,rfl⟩
  exact h x

theorem doomed_example :
    (1:ℝ)*(1-(9/10)^3)/(1-9/10)-20*(9/10)^2 = -1349/100 := by norm_num

theorem negative_reward_extension_reverses :
    -(1:ℝ)-(9/10) > -(1:ℝ)-(9/10)-(9/10)^2 := by norm_num

theorem two_step_slope_bound (discount cost penalty : ℝ)
    (hd : 0 ≤ discount) (hd1 : discount ≤ 1) (hc : 0 ≤ cost) (hp : 0 ≤ penalty) :
    max (-cost-discount*penalty) (-cost-discount*cost-discount^2*penalty) ≤
      -penalty*discount^2 := by
  have hprod := mul_nonneg hp (mul_nonneg hd (sub_nonneg.mpr hd1))
  have hdc := mul_nonneg hd hc
  apply max_le <;> nlinarith

theorem slow_slope_strictly_better (discount cost penalty : ℝ) (hd : 0 < discount) :
    -cost-discount*penalty < -cost-discount*cost-discount^2*penalty ↔
      cost < penalty*(1-discount) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    nlinarith
  · intro h
    nlinarith

theorem negative_reward_slope_bound_false (discount cost penalty : ℝ)
    (hd : 0 < discount) (hc : 0 < cost) :
    -cost*(1+discount+discount^2)-penalty*discount^2 <
      -cost-discount*cost-discount^2*penalty := by
  have h := mul_pos hc (sq_pos_of_pos hd)
  nlinarith

def binaryValue (penalty : ℝ) (isUnsafe : Bool) : ℝ := if isUnsafe then 1-penalty else 0

theorem every_binary_optimizer_safe_iff (penalty : ℝ) :
    (∀ action, (∀ other, binaryValue penalty other ≤ binaryValue penalty action) →
      action=false) ↔ 1 < penalty := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hn
    have hp : penalty ≤ 1 := le_of_not_gt hn
    have ht : ∀ other, binaryValue penalty other ≤ binaryValue penalty true := by
      intro other
      cases other <;> simp [binaryValue] <;> linarith
    have := h true ht
    contradiction
  · intro hp action hmax
    cases action
    · rfl
    · have := hmax false
      simp only [binaryValue,Bool.false_eq_true,if_false,if_true] at this
      linarith

theorem equality_retains_unsafe_optimizer :
    ∀ other, binaryValue 1 other ≤ binaryValue 1 true := by
  intro other
  cases other <;> norm_num [binaryValue]

theorem arrival_time_example : -(20:ℝ)*(9/10)^3 = -729/50 ∧
    -(20:ℝ)*(9/10)^0 = -20 ∧ -(20:ℝ) < -(20:ℝ)*(9/10)^3 := by norm_num

theorem contraction_residual_bound {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X]
    (operator : X → X) (fixed approximate : X) (discount residual : ℝ)
    (hd1 : discount < 1)
    (hcontract : ∀ x y, dist (operator x) (operator y) ≤ discount*dist x y)
    (hfixed : operator fixed=fixed) (hresidual : dist approximate (operator approximate) ≤ residual) :
    dist approximate fixed ≤ residual/(1-discount) := by
  have htriangle := dist_triangle approximate (operator approximate) fixed
  have hc := hcontract approximate fixed
  rw [hfixed] at hc
  apply (le_div_iff₀ (by linarith : 0 < 1-discount)).mpr
  nlinarith

theorem bellman_residual_example : (2/1000:ℝ)/(1-95/100)=1/25 := by norm_num

end SafeLearning.CompleteModulesValues
